{"body":"**Deferred scope** from PR #193 (Snowflake key-pair auth).\n\nv1 key-pair auth (`_private_key_der` in `backend/app/datasources/snowflake.py`) loads the PEM private key with `password=None` — i.e. **unencrypted keys only**. Many orgs use passphrase-protected keys.\n\n**Done when:** an encrypted PEM key authenticates. The wrinkle: the passphrase is itself a secret, but a connection has a single `secret_ref` (the key). Options: (a) a second SecretStore entry for the passphrase, (b) a combined secret payload (key + passphrase JSON), (c) require unencrypted keys (status quo). Decide the model before implementing.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Connection create/edit accepts a passphrase-protected (PKCS#8) private key + passphrase (stored in SecretStore, never logged)\n- [ ] Test-connection AND a real suite run succeed against live Snowflake using an encrypted key\n- [ ] Unencrypted key path regression-tested (no behavior change)\n\n_(AC added at v1.1 planning, 2026-07-04.)_","labels":["enhancement","priority/P3"],"milestone":"v1.1 Week 1 — Snowflake close-out + PATs","title":"Snowflake key-pair: support encrypted (passphrase-protected) private keys"}

{"body":"**Review follow-up** from PR #193 (Snowflake key-pair auth).\n\n`SnowflakeCheckRunner.run_checks` passes the key-pair credential to GX via `add_snowflake(kwargs={\"connect_args\": {\"private_key\": der}})`. GX 1.17 **deprecates** this and recommends a direct `private_key=` argument to `add_snowflake()`. It is functionally correct today (verified the base64 round-trip is safe for DER PKCS8 keys) but emits a `DeprecationWarning` on every key-pair suite run and rides GX-internal behaviour.\n\n**Done when:** the GX runner uses the supported `private_key=` form (or whatever GX's non-deprecated key-pair API is at the pinned version), validated during the live-Snowflake smoke. Only the GX runner is affected — the adapter `test` + profiler paths use `create_engine` directly and are unaffected.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Snowflake GX runner no longer passes the deprecated `kwargs['connect_args']` private_key path (uses the GX-supported mechanism)\n- [ ] Live key-pair suite run green with zero deprecation warnings in logs\n- [ ] Covered by a test pinning the new construction\n\n_(AC added at v1.1 planning, 2026-07-04.)_","labels":["priority/P3","refactor"],"milestone":"v1.1 Week 1 — Snowflake close-out + PATs","title":"Snowflake key-pair: migrate GX runner off deprecated kwargs['connect_args'] private_key path"}

1	"""Snowflake datasource adapter (GX Core 1.17).
2	
3	All Great-Expectations-specific machinery for Snowflake lives here, behind the
4	`CheckRunner` seam in ``base.py`` — per CLAUDE.md, the GX version-specific API
5	must not leak into the suite / check / result layer (GX v1 has drifted across
6	point releases).
7	
8	The full GX chain (``add_snowflake`` → ``add_table_asset`` →
9	``add_batch_definition_whole_table`` → ``ValidationDefinition.run``) connects to
10	Snowflake at asset-build time, so ``run_checks`` cannot run without a live
11	warehouse. Tests therefore exercise the GX-free parts directly — config
12	validation, connection-string building, the snake_case→GX-class translation,
13	and the GX-result→`CheckOutcome` mapping (fed a canned result) — and inject a
14	fake `CheckRunner` elsewhere. End-to-end validation against a real Snowflake DEV
15	warehouse is a tracked follow-up.
16	"""

42	    "SnowflakeCheckRunner",
43	    "SnowflakeConfig",
44	    "SnowflakeConnectionAdapter",
45	    "UnknownExpectationError",

47	    "_to_gx_expectation",

49	    "build_connection_string",
50	    "build_snowflake_runner",

52	]

54	
55	class SnowflakeConfig(BaseModel):
56	    """Non-secret Snowflake connection config (the password comes from secrets).
57	
58	    Maps from ``Connection.config``. ``schema`` is aliased to ``schema_`` to
59	    avoid shadowing pydantic's ``BaseModel.schema``.
60	    """
61	
62	    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True, extra="forbid")
63	
64	    account: str
65	    user: str
66	    database: str
67	    schema_: str = Field(alias="schema")
68	    warehouse: str
69	    role: str | None = None
70	    # Auth method. 'password' (default — back-compat for existing configs that
71	    # carry no auth_type) puts the password in the DSN. 'key_pair' authenticates
72	    # with an RSA private key: the secret is the **PEM private key** (v1: an
73	    # unencrypted key) passed as `private_key` connect-arg, and the DSN carries
74	    # no password. Both share the same SecretStore `secret_ref`.
75	    auth_type: Literal["password", "key_pair"] = "password"
76	
77	
78	def _private_key_der(pem: str) -> bytes:
79	    """Load a PEM RSA private key (v1: unencrypted) → DER PKCS8 bytes.
80	
81	    snowflake-connector's `private_key` connect-arg wants DER PKCS8, not PEM.
82	    Encrypted keys (passphrase) are a follow-up — v1 key-pair uses unencrypted keys.
83	    """
84	    key = serialization.load_pem_private_key(pem.encode(), password=None)
85	    return key.private_bytes(
86	        encoding=serialization.Encoding.DER,
87	        format=serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,
88	        encryption_algorithm=serialization.NoEncryption(),
89	    )
90	
91	
92	def build_connection_string(config: SnowflakeConfig, secret: str) -> str:
93	    """Assemble a snowflake-sqlalchemy URL. User/password/params are URL-encoded.
94	
95	    For key-pair auth the DSN carries **no password** (the key rides in
96	    connect-args, see `build_connect_args`); ``secret`` is then ignored here.
97	    """
98	    params = {"warehouse": config.warehouse}
99	    if config.role:
100	        params["role"] = config.role
101	    query = "&".join(f"{key}={quote_plus(value)}" for key, value in params.items())
102	    credentials = (
103	        quote_plus(config.user)
104	        if config.auth_type == "key_pair"
105	        else f"{quote_plus(config.user)}:{quote_plus(secret)}"
106	    )
107	    return f"snowflake://{credentials}@{config.account}/{config.database}/{config.schema_}?{query}"
108	
109	
110	def build_connect_args(config: SnowflakeConfig, secret: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
111	    """SQLAlchemy `connect_args` carrying the key-pair credential, if any.
112	
113	    Empty for password auth (the password is in the DSN). For key-pair, the
114	    loaded DER private key under `private_key` (the snowflake-connector arg).
115	    """
116	    if config.auth_type == "key_pair":
117	        return {"private_key": _private_key_der(secret)}
118	    return {}
119	
120	
121	class SnowflakeCheckRunner:
122	    """`CheckRunner` for Snowflake. Building the asset connects to the warehouse."""
123	
124	    def __init__(self, config: SnowflakeConfig, secret: str) -> None:
125	        self._config = config
126	        self._connection_string = build_connection_string(config, secret)
127	        # Key-pair auth passes the private key as a SQLAlchemy connect-arg (GX
128	        # forwards `kwargs` to the engine); empty for password auth.
129	        self._connect_args = build_connect_args(config, secret)
130	
131	    def run_checks(
132	        self,
133	        *,
134	        table: str,
135	        schema: str | None,
136	        checks: list[CheckSpec],
137	        index_columns: list[str] | None = None,
138	    ) -> SuiteOutcome:
139	        context = gx.get_context(mode="ephemeral")
140	        add_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {}
141	        if self._connect_args:
142	            # GX 1.17 deprecates passing private_key via kwargs['connect_args'] in
143	            # favour of a direct private_key= arg; this works today but should
144	            # migrate during the live-Snowflake smoke (#195). The adapter test +
145	            # profiler paths use create_engine directly, so they're unaffected.
146	            add_kwargs["kwargs"] = {"connect_args": self._connect_args}
147	        datasource = context.data_sources.add_snowflake(
148	            name=f"sf-{table}",
149	            connection_string=self._connection_string,
150	            **add_kwargs,
151	        )
152	        asset = datasource.add_table_asset(
153	            name=table,
154	            table_name=table,
155	            schema_name=schema or self._config.schema_,
156	        )
157	        # The table asset resolves its own batch, so no batch_parameters; the
158	        # ephemeral context makes the fixed suite/vd names safe across runs.
159	        batch_definition = asset.add_batch_definition_whole_table(name="whole_table")
160	        return run_expectations(
161	            context,
162	            batch_definition=batch_definition,
163	            checks=checks,
164	            name=f"suite-{table}",
165	            index_columns=index_columns,
166	        )
167	
168	    def run_monitors(
169	        self, *, table: str, schema: str | None, monitors: list[MonitorSpec]
170	    ) -> list[CheckOutcome]:
171	        """Evaluate freshness/volume monitors via scalar SQL aggregates (no GX).
172	
173	        Opens one SQLAlchemy connection over the same DSN the GX path uses; Snowflake
174	        addresses the target as ``schema.table`` (the database is in the DSN), so no
175	        catalog. A connection-level failure (can't reach the warehouse) propagates,
176	        failing the run like the GX path; a bad monitor errors only itself."""
177	        from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text
178	
179	        engine = create_engine(self._connection_string, connect_args=self._connect_args or {})
180	        try:
181	            with engine.connect() as conn:
182	                return evaluate_monitors(
183	                    lambda sql: conn.execute(text(sql)).scalar(),
184	                    table=table,
185	                    schema=schema or self._config.schema_,
186	                    catalog=None,
187	                    monitors=monitors,
188	                )
189	        finally:
190	            engine.dispose()
191	
192	
193	def build_snowflake_runner(
194	    *,
195	    config: dict[str, Any],
196	    secret_ref: str | None,
197	    secret_store: SecretStore,
198	) -> SnowflakeCheckRunner:
199	    """Build a runner from a `Connection` row's config + secret_ref.
200	
201	    Takes primitives (not the ORM model) to keep the adapter decoupled from the
202	    DB layer.
203	    """
204	    if not secret_ref:
205	        raise ValueError("Snowflake connection requires secret_ref for the password / private key")
206	    sf_config = SnowflakeConfig.model_validate(config)
207	    secret = secret_store.get(secret_ref)
208	    return SnowflakeCheckRunner(sf_config, secret)
209	
210	
211	# Snowflake connector timeouts (seconds) for the connectivity test — fail fast
212	# rather than hanging the request thread on an unreachable account.
213	_TEST_LOGIN_TIMEOUT = 10
214	_TEST_NETWORK_TIMEOUT = 10
215	
216	
217	class SnowflakeConnectionAdapter:
218	    """`ConnectionAdapter` for Snowflake — config validation + a SELECT 1 test."""
219	
220	    def validate_config(self, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> SnowflakeConfig:
221	        return SnowflakeConfig.model_validate(raw)
222	
223	    def test(self, raw: dict[str, Any], secret: str) -> None:
224	        """Open a connection and run ``SELECT 1``; raise on any failure.
225	
226	        Deliberately GX-free — a lightweight connectivity probe, not a suite run.
227	        """
228	        from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text
229	
230	        config = self.validate_config(raw)
231	        engine = create_engine(
232	            build_connection_string(config, secret),
233	            connect_args={
234	                "login_timeout": _TEST_LOGIN_TIMEOUT,
235	                "network_timeout": _TEST_NETWORK_TIMEOUT,
236	                **build_connect_args(config, secret),
237	            },
238	        )
239	        try:
240	            with engine.connect() as conn:
241	                conn.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
242	        finally:
243	            engine.dispose()
244

3	/**
4	 * Single source of truth for the add-connection form's per-type fields.
5	 *
6	 * Each type declares its config text fields and either an auth-type select (the
7	 * first option is the default) or a single secret. v1 only declares the auth
8	 * modes the backend accepts — ADLS Gen2's managed-identity and S3's IAM-role
9	 * modes are deferred, so they're absent here; every declared mode needs a secret.

14	  label: string;

24	  multilineSecret?: boolean;

1	import { App, Button, Flex, Form, Input, Select, Tag, Typography } from 'antd';
2	import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
3	
4	import {
5	  CONNECTION_ENVS,
6	  CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS,
7	  type Connection,
8	  type ConnectionCreate,
9	  type ConnectionType,
10	  createConnection,
11	  ENV_COLORS,
12	  envLabel,
13	  updateConnection,
14	} from '../../api/connections';
15	import { ConnectionTypeFields } from './ConnectionTypeFields';
16	import { initialConfigForType } from './connectionFormSpec';
17	
18	interface FormValues {
19	  name: string;
20	  env: ConnectionCreate['env'];
21	  config?: Record<string, unknown>;
22	  secret?: string;
23	}
24	
25	/**
26	 * Create or edit a connection — the form body shared by the `/connections/new`
27	 * page (a type is picked first, then this renders) and the `/connections/:id/edit`
28	 * page (the drawer is retired in W6, ADR 0022). `connection === undefined` is
29	 * create mode (env is chosen + the credential is captured); editing locks type +
30	 * env (the backend `ConnectionUpdate` rejects changing them) and omits the secret
31	 * — credential rotation is the separate Re-auth flow.
32	 */
33	export function ConnectionForm({
34	  type,
35	  connection,
36	  onSaved,
37	  onCancel,
38	}: {
39	  /** The connection type — picked on the new page, fixed from the row on edit. */
40	  type: ConnectionType;
41	  connection?: Connection;
42	  /** Called with the saved connection (created or updated). */
43	  onSaved: (connection: Connection) => void;
44	  onCancel: () => void;
45	}) {
46	  const { message } = App.useApp();
47	  const [form] = Form.useForm<FormValues>();
48	  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
49	  const isEdit = connection !== undefined;
50	
51	  // Seed the form: an edit prefills name + config; a create seeds the new type's
52	  // config defaults (e.g. the auth-type) and clears any fields left over from a
53	  // previously-picked type. Re-runs on `type`/`connection` so re-picking a type
54	  // on the new page can't leak the prior type's fields.
55	  useEffect(() => {
56	    form.resetFields();
57	    if (connection) {
58	      form.setFieldsValue({ name: connection.name, config: connection.config });
59	    } else {
60	      form.setFieldsValue({ config: initialConfigForType(type) });
61	    }
62	  }, [type, connection, form]);
63	
64	  const onFinish = async (values: FormValues) => {
65	    setSubmitting(true);
66	    try {
67	      const saved = isEdit
68	        ? await updateConnection(connection.id, {
69	            name: values.name,
70	            config: values.config ?? {},
71	          })
72	        : await createConnection({
73	            name: values.name,
74	            type,
75	            env: values.env,
76	            config: values.config ?? {},
77	            secret: values.secret || undefined,
78	          });
79	      message.success(`Connection “${values.name}” ${isEdit ? 'updated' : 'created'}`);
80	      onSaved(saved);
81	    } catch (err) {
82	      message.error(
83	        `${isEdit ? 'Update' : 'Create'} failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`,
84	      );
85	    } finally {
86	      setSubmitting(false);
87	    }
88	  };
89	
90	  return (
91	    <Form form={form} layout="vertical" onFinish={onFinish} requiredMark="optional">
92	      <Form.Item name="name" label="Name" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
93	        <Input />
94	      </Form.Item>
95	      {isEdit ? (
96	        // Type + env are fixed once a connection is created — show, don't edit.
97	        <>
98	          <Form.Item label="Type">
99	            <Typography.Text>{CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[type]}</Typography.Text>
100	          </Form.Item>
101	          <Form.Item label="Environment">
102	            <Tag color={ENV_COLORS[connection.env]}>{envLabel(connection.env)}</Tag>
103	          </Form.Item>
104	        </>
105	      ) : (
106	        <Form.Item name="env" label="Environment" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
107	          <Select
108	            options={CONNECTION_ENVS.map((e) => ({ value: e, label: envLabel(e) }))}
109	            placeholder="Select an environment"
110	          />
111	        </Form.Item>
112	      )}
113	      <ConnectionTypeFields type={type} form={form} showSecret={!isEdit} />
114	      <Flex justify="end" gap={8}>
115	        <Button onClick={onCancel}>{isEdit ? 'Cancel' : 'Back'}</Button>
116	        <Button type="primary" htmlType="submit" loading={submitting}>
117	          {isEdit ? 'Save' : 'Create'}
118	        </Button>
119	      </Flex>
120	    </Form>
121	  );
122	}

1	import { Form, Input, Select, type FormInstance } from 'antd';
2	
3	import type { ConnectionType } from '../../api/connections';
4	import { CONNECTION_FORM_SPECS, type TextField } from './connectionFormSpec';
5	
6	/**
7	 * Renders the type-specific config + secret form fields from CONNECTION_FORM_SPECS.
8	 * Config fields are namespaced under `config` (name={['config','account']}) so the
9	 * drawer submits `config` as one object; the write-only credential is `secret`.
10	 */
11	
12	const requiredRule = [{ required: true }];
13	
14	function ConfigTextField({ field }: { field: TextField }) {
15	  return (
16	    <Form.Item
17	      name={['config', field.name]}
18	      label={field.optional ? `${field.label} (optional)` : field.label}
19	      rules={field.optional ? undefined : requiredRule}
20	    >
21	      <Input />
22	    </Form.Item>
23	  );
24	}
25	
26	function SecretField({ label, multiline = false }: { label: string; multiline?: boolean }) {
27	  return (
28	    <Form.Item name="secret" label={label} rules={requiredRule}>
29	      {multiline ? (
30	        <Input.TextArea rows={4} autoComplete="off" />
31	      ) : (
32	        <Input.Password autoComplete="off" />
33	      )}
34	    </Form.Item>
35	  );
36	}
37	
38	export function ConnectionTypeFields({
39	  type,
40	  form,
41	  showSecret = true,
42	}: {
43	  type: ConnectionType;
44	  form: FormInstance;
45	  /** Edit mode omits the secret — credential rotation is the Re-auth flow. */
46	  showSecret?: boolean;
47	}) {
48	  const spec = CONNECTION_FORM_SPECS[type];
49	  const authType = Form.useWatch(['config', 'auth_type'], form) as string | undefined;
50	  const activeAuth = spec.auth?.find((a) => a.value === authType) ?? spec.auth?.[0];
51	
52	  return (
53	    <>
54	      {spec.textFields.map((f) => (
55	        <ConfigTextField key={f.name} field={f} />
56	      ))}
57	
58	      {spec.auth && (
59	        <Form.Item name={['config', 'auth_type']} label="Auth type" rules={requiredRule}>
60	          <Select options={spec.auth.map((a) => ({ value: a.value, label: a.label }))} />
61	        </Form.Item>
62	      )}
63	
64	      {activeAuth?.extraField && <ConfigTextField field={activeAuth.extraField} />}
65	
66	      {showSecret &&
67	        (activeAuth ? (
68	          <SecretField label={activeAuth.secretLabel} multiline={activeAuth.multilineSecret} />
69	        ) : (
70	          spec.secretLabel && <SecretField label={spec.secretLabel} />
71	        ))}
72	    </>
73	  );
74	}

1	import { App, Form, Input, Modal } from 'antd';
2	import { useState } from 'react';
3	
4	import { type Connection, reauthConnection } from '../../api/connections';
5	
6	/**
7	 * Rotate a connection's stored credential. The backend verifies the new
8	 * credential against the datasource, so a bad value surfaces as an error and the
9	 * old credential is unaffected. `connection === null` means the modal is closed.
10	 */
11	export function ReauthModal({
12	  connection,
13	  onClose,
14	  onDone,
15	}: {
16	  connection: Connection | null;
17	  onClose: () => void;
18	  /** Called after a successful rotation (so the list can refresh `has_secret`). */
19	  onDone: () => void;
20	}) {
21	  const { message } = App.useApp();
22	  const [form] = Form.useForm<{ secret: string }>();
23	  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
24	
25	  const onOk = async () => {
26	    if (!connection) return;
27	    // antd's Modal `onOk` doesn't catch a rejected handler, so guard the
28	    // validation rejection here (errors render inline) rather than letting it
29	    // escape as an unhandled promise rejection.
30	    let secret: string;
31	    try {
32	      ({ secret } = await form.validateFields());
33	    } catch {
34	      return;
35	    }
36	    setSubmitting(true);
37	    try {
38	      await reauthConnection(connection.id, secret);
39	      message.success(`${connection.name}: credential rotated`);
40	      form.resetFields();
41	      onDone();
42	    } catch (err) {
43	      message.error(`Re-auth failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
44	    } finally {
45	      setSubmitting(false);
46	    }
47	  };
48	
49	  return (
50	    <Modal
51	      title={connection ? `Re-authenticate “${connection.name}”` : 'Re-authenticate'}
52	      open={connection !== null}
53	      onOk={onOk}
54	      onCancel={onClose}
55	      confirmLoading={submitting}
56	      okText="Rotate credential"
57	      destroyOnHidden
58	    >
59	      <Form form={form} layout="vertical">
60	        <Form.Item
61	          name="secret"
62	          label="New credential"
63	          rules={[{ required: true }]}
64	          extra="Rotates the stored credential and verifies it against the datasource."
65	        >
66	          <Input.Password autoComplete="off" />
67	        </Form.Item>
68	      </Form>
69	    </Modal>
70	  );
71	}
72

  "new_string": "def _parse_key_pair_secret(secret: str) -> tuple[str, bytes | None]:\n    \"\"\"Split a key-pair secret payload into (PEM key, passphrase bytes or None).\n\n    Two shapes are accepted: a bare PEM string (an unencrypted key — the\n    original v1 form, unchanged) or a JSON object\n    ``{\"private_key\": \"<PEM>\", \"passphrase\": \"<str>\"}`` for passphrase-protected\n    keys. One SecretStore entry carries both parts so the connection keeps a\n    single `secret_ref` and rotation via re-auth stays atomic (#194).\n\n    Error messages never include payload content — they can carry key material.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not secret.lstrip().startswith(\"{\"):\n        return secret, None\n    try:\n        payload = json.loads(secret)\n    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:\n        raise ValueError(\"key-pair secret payload is not valid JSON\") from exc\n    if not isinstance(payload, dict) or not isinstance(payload.get(\"private_key\"), str):\n        raise ValueError(\"key-pair secret payload must carry a 'private_key' string\")\n    passphrase = payload.get(\"passphrase\")\n    if passphrase is not None and not isinstance(passphrase, str):\n        raise ValueError(\"key-pair secret 'passphrase' must be a string\")\n    return payload[\"private_key\"], passphrase.encode() if passphrase else None\n\n\ndef _private_key_der(secret: str) -> bytes:\n    \"\"\"Load the key-pair secret → DER PKCS8 bytes.\n\n    snowflake-connector's `private_key` connect-arg wants DER PKCS8, not PEM.\n    Passphrase-protected keys arrive as the JSON payload\n    (see `_parse_key_pair_secret`); bare PEM means an unencrypted key.\n    \"\"\"\n    pem, passphrase = _parse_key_pair_secret(secret)\n    try:\n        key = serialization.load_pem_private_key(pem.encode(), password=passphrase)\n    except TypeError as exc:\n        # cryptography reports passphrase-presence mismatches (encrypted key\n        # without a passphrase, or a passphrase for an unencrypted key) as\n        # TypeError; normalise to ValueError so callers see one failure type.\n        # Its messages state the mismatch only — no key/passphrase material.\n        raise ValueError(str(exc)) from exc\n    return key.private_bytes(\n        encoding=serialization.Encoding.DER,\n        format=serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,\n        encryption_algorithm=serialization.NoEncryption(),\n    )"

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/src/components/connections/ReauthModal.tsx",
  "content": "import { App, Form, Input, Modal } from 'antd';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nimport { type Connection, reauthConnection } from '../../api/connections';\nimport { activeAuthOption, composeSecret } from './connectionFormSpec';\n\n/**\n * Rotate a connection's stored credential. The backend verifies the new\n * credential against the datasource, so a bad value surfaces as an error and the\n * old credential is unaffected. The fields follow the connection's auth mode\n * (from CONNECTION_FORM_SPECS): a multi-line input for PEM keys, plus the\n * optional passphrase for key-pair modes — composed the same way as on create\n * (`composeSecret`). `connection === null` means the modal is closed.\n */\nexport function ReauthModal({\n  connection,\n  onClose,\n  onDone,\n}: {\n  connection: Connection | null;\n  onClose: () => void;\n  /** Called after a successful rotation (so the list can refresh `has_secret`). */\n  onDone: () => void;\n}) {\n  const { message } = App.useApp();\n  const [form] = Form.useForm<{ secret: string; secretPassphrase?: string }>();\n  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);\n\n  const auth = connection ? activeAuthOption(connection.type, connection.config) : undefined;\n\n  const onOk = async () => {\n    if (!connection) return;\n    // antd's Modal `onOk` doesn't catch a rejected handler, so guard the\n    // validation rejection here (errors render inline) rather than letting it\n    // escape as an unhandled promise rejection.\n    let secret: string;\n    let secretPassphrase: string | undefined;\n    try {\n      ({ secret, secretPassphrase } = await form.validateFields());\n    } catch {\n      return;\n    }\n    setSubmitting(true);\n    try {\n      await reauthConnection(connection.id, composeSecret(secret, secretPassphrase));\n      message.success(`${connection.name}: credential rotated`);\n      form.resetFields();\n      onDone();\n    } catch (err) {\n      message.error(`Re-auth failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);\n    } finally {\n      setSubmitting(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <Modal\n      title={connection ? `Re-authenticate “${connection.name}”` : 'Re-authenticate'}\n      open={connection !== null}\n      onOk={onOk}\n      onCancel={onClose}\n      confirmLoading={submitting}\n      okText=\"Rotate credential\"\n      destroyOnHidden\n    >\n      <Form form={form} layout=\"vertical\">\n        <Form.Item\n          name=\"secret\"\n          label={auth ? `New ${auth.secretLabel.toLowerCase()}` : 'New credential'}\n          rules={[{ required: true }]}\n          extra=\"Rotates the stored credential and verifies it against the datasource.\"\n        >\n          {auth?.multilineSecret ? (\n            <Input.TextArea rows={4} autoComplete=\"off\" />\n          ) : (\n            <Input.Password autoComplete=\"off\" />\n          )}\n        </Form.Item>\n        {auth?.passphraseLabel && (\n          <Form.Item\n            name=\"secretPassphrase\"\n            label={`${auth.passphraseLabel} (optional)`}\n            extra=\"Only for passphrase-protected keys; leave blank for an unencrypted key.\"\n          >\n            <Input.Password autoComplete=\"off\" />\n          </Form.Item>\n        )}\n      </Form>\n    </Modal>\n  );\n}\n"
}

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/tests/datasources/test_snowflake.py",
  "old_string": "def _rsa_pem() -> str:\n    \"\"\"An unencrypted PEM RSA private key for key-pair auth tests.\"\"\"\n    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization\n    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa\n\n    key = rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)\n    return key.private_bytes(\n        encoding=serialization.Encoding.PEM,\n        format=serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,\n        encryption_algorithm=serialization.NoEncryption(),\n    ).decode()",
  "new_string": "def _rsa_pem() -> str:\n    \"\"\"An unencrypted PEM RSA private key for key-pair auth tests.\"\"\"\n    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization\n    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa\n\n    key = rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)\n    return key.private_bytes(\n        encoding=serialization.Encoding.PEM,\n        format=serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,\n        encryption_algorithm=serialization.NoEncryption(),\n    ).decode()\n\n\ndef _rsa_pem_encrypted(passphrase: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A passphrase-protected (PKCS#8) PEM RSA private key.\"\"\"\n    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization\n    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa\n\n    key = rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)\n    return key.private_bytes(\n        encoding=serialization.Encoding.PEM,\n        format=serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,\n        encryption_algorithm=serialization.BestAvailableEncryption(passphrase.encode()),\n    ).decode()\n\n\ndef _key_pair_payload(pem: str, passphrase: str | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The combined key-pair secret payload (#194) as the frontend composes it.\"\"\"\n    import json\n\n    payload: dict[str, str] = {\"private_key\": pem}\n    if passphrase is not None:\n        payload[\"passphrase\"] = passphrase\n    return json.dumps(payload)"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Live verification for #194 — encrypted (passphrase-protected) Snowflake key-pair auth.\n\nSteps:\n 1. Generate a passphrase-protected PKCS#8 RSA key locally.\n 2. Register its public key on the harness user's spare RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2 slot\n    (primary slot untouched).\n 3. adapter.test() with the combined {private_key, passphrase} payload  → SELECT 1.\n 4. SnowflakeCheckRunner.run_checks() (the GX path) with the same payload → suite run.\n 5. Negative: wrong passphrase → clean ValueError before any connection.\n 6. Unset RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2 (cleanup) — runs even if verification fails.\n\nCredentials come from env vars (source ~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/secrets.sh);\nnothing secret is printed or persisted.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport secrets as pysecrets\nimport sys\n\nfrom cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization\nfrom cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.path.expanduser(\"~/Coding/Python/DataQ\"))\n\nfrom backend.app.datasources.base import CheckSpec  # noqa: E402\nfrom backend.app.datasources.snowflake import (  # noqa: E402\n    SnowflakeCheckRunner,\n    SnowflakeConfig,\n    SnowflakeConnectionAdapter,\n)\n\nACCOUNT = os.environ[\"SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT\"]\nUSER = os.environ[\"SNOWFLAKE_USER\"]\nPASSWORD = os.environ[\"SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD\"]\nDATABASE = \"DATAQ_DB\"\nWAREHOUSE = \"DATAQ_WH\"\nROLE = \"ACCOUNTADMIN\"\n\nPASSPHRASE = pysecrets.token_urlsafe(16)\n\n# ── 1. generate the encrypted key ────────────────────────────────────────────\nkey = rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)\nencrypted_pem = key.private_bytes(\n    encoding=serialization.Encoding.PEM,\n    format=serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,\n    encryption_algorithm=serialization.BestAvailableEncryption(PASSPHRASE.encode()),\n).decode()\nassert \"ENCRYPTED\" in encrypted_pem.splitlines()[0], \"key must actually be encrypted\"\npublic_b64 = (\n    key.public_key()\n    .public_bytes(\n        encoding=serialization.Encoding.DER,\n        format=serialization.PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo,\n    )\n    .hex()\n)  # placeholder; replaced below with base64\nimport base64  # noqa: E402\n\npublic_b64 = base64.b64encode(\n    key.public_key().public_bytes(\n        encoding=serialization.Encoding.DER,\n        format=serialization.PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo,\n    )\n).decode()\n\n# ── 2. register the public key on the spare slot (password auth) ─────────────\nimport snowflake.connector  # noqa: E402\n\nadmin = snowflake.connector.connect(\n    account=ACCOUNT, user=USER, password=PASSWORD, role=ROLE, login_timeout=30\n)\ntry:\n    cur = admin.cursor()\n    cur.execute(f\"ALTER USER {USER} SET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2 = '{public_b64}'\")\n    print(\"[2] RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2 registered\")\n\n    # pick a table for the suite run\n    cur.execute(\n        f\"SELECT table_schema, table_name FROM {DATABASE}.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES \"\n        \"WHERE table_type = 'BASE TABLE' ORDER BY row_count DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1\"\n    )\n    row = cur.fetchone()\n    assert row, \"no table found in DATAQ_DB\"\n    schema_name, table_name = row\n    print(f\"[2] target table: {schema_name}.{table_name}\")\n\n    payload = json.dumps({\"private_key\": encrypted_pem, \"passphrase\": PASSPHRASE})\n    config = {\n        \"account\": ACCOUNT,\n        \"user\": USER,\n        \"database\": DATABASE,\n        \"schema\": schema_name,\n        \"warehouse\": WAREHOUSE,\n        \"role\": ROLE,\n        \"auth_type\": \"key_pair\",\n    }\n\n    # ── 3. adapter test path ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    SnowflakeConnectionAdapter().test(config, payload)\n    print(\"[3] adapter.test() with encrypted key + passphrase: OK\")\n\n    # ── 4. GX suite run path ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    runner = SnowflakeCheckRunner(SnowflakeConfig.model_validate(config), payload)\n    outcome = runner.run_checks(\n        table=table_name,\n        schema=schema_name,\n        checks=[\n            CheckSpec(\"expect_table_row_count_to_be_between\", {\"min_value\": 0}),\n        ],\n    )\n    print(f\"[4] GX suite run: success={outcome.success} checks={len(outcome.results)}\")\n    assert outcome.success, f\"suite run failed: {outcome}\"\n\n    # ── 5. negative: wrong passphrase ────────────────────────────────────────\n    bad = json.dumps({\"private_key\": encrypted_pem, \"passphrase\": \"wrong-\" + PASSPHRASE})\n    try:\n        SnowflakeConnectionAdapter().test(config, bad)\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        assert PASSPHRASE not in str(exc)\n        print(\"[5] wrong passphrase → clean ValueError (no secret leaked): OK\")\n    else:\n        raise AssertionError(\"wrong passphrase unexpectedly succeeded\")\n\n    print(\"\\nLIVE VERIFY #194: ALL GREEN\")\nfinally:\n    # ── 6. cleanup ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    admin.cursor().execute(f\"ALTER USER {USER} UNSET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2\")\n    print(\"[6] RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2 unset (cleanup)\")\n    admin.close()\n"

class ConnectionDetails(FluentBaseModel):
    """
    Information needed to connect to a Snowflake database.
    Alternative to a connection string.

    https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/python-connector/sqlalchemy#additional-connection-parameters
    """

    account: AccountIdentifier
    user: str
    password: Union[ConfigStr, str]
    database: str = pydantic.Field(
        ...,
        description="`database` that the Datasource is mapped to.",
    )
    schema_: str = pydantic.Field(
        ..., alias="schema", description="`schema` that the Datasource is mapped to."
    )  # schema is a reserved attr in BaseModel
    warehouse: str
    role: str
    numpy: bool = False

    @classmethod
    def required_fields(cls) -> list[str]:
        """Returns the required fields for this model as defined in the schema."""
        return cls.schema()["required"]

    class Config:
        @staticmethod
        def schema_extra(schema: dict, model: type[ConnectionDetails]) -> None:
            schema["properties"]["account"] = AccountIdentifier.get_schema()

        """
        If connection_string is a SnowflakeDsn,
        check for required query parameters according to `REQUIRED_QUERY_PARAMS`.
        """
        if not isinstance(connection_string, (SnowflakeDsn, ConfigUri)):
            return connection_string

            query_params: dict[str, list[str]] = urllib.parse.parse_qs(connection_string.query)

            for key in REQUIRED_QUERY_PARAMS:

                msg=f"missing {', '.join(sorted(missing_keys))}",

    def _build_engine_with_connect_args(
        self,
        url: SnowflakeURL | None = None,
        connect_args: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> sqlalchemy.Engine:
        if not url:
            url_args = self._get_url_args()
            url_args.update(kwargs)

            password = url_args.get("password")
            if isinstance(password, str):
                url_args["password"] = quote(password)

        else:

        engine_kwargs: dict[Literal["url", "connect_args"], Any] = {}
        if connect_args:

                    " ignoring password and using private_key for authentication"
                )
                # assume the private_key is base64 encoded
                connect_args["private_key"] = base64.standard_b64decode(private_key)

            engine_kwargs["connect_args"] = connect_args

        engine_kwargs["url"] = url

        return sa.create_engine(**engine_kwargs)  # type: ignore[misc] # FIXME CoP

    def _get_connect_args(self) -> dict[str, str | bool]:
        excluded_fields: set[str] = set(SQLDatasource.__fields__.keys())
        # dump as json dict to force serialization of things like AnyUrl
        return self._json_dict(exclude=excluded_fields, exclude_none=True)

    def _get_snowflake_partner_application(self) -> str:
        """
        This is used to set the application query parameter in the Snowflake connection URL,
        which provides attribution to GX for the Snowflake Partner program.
        """

        # This import is here to avoid a circular import
        from great_expectations.data_context import CloudDataContext

        if isinstance(self._data_context, CloudDataContext):
            return SNOWFLAKE_PARTNER_APPLICATION_CLOUD
        return SNOWFLAKE_PARTNER_APPLICATION_OSS

    def _get_url_args(self) -> dict[str, str | bool]:
        excluded_fields: set[str] = set(SQLDatasource.__fields__.keys())
        # dump as json dict to force serialization of things like AnyUrl
        return self._json_dict(exclude=excluded_fields, exclude_none=True)

    @override
    def get_execution_engine(self) -> SqlAlchemyExecutionEngine:
        """

  "content": "\"\"\"Probe: which private_key value form works with GX 1.17 add_snowflake(kwargs) live.\n\nTries the non-deprecated KeyPairConnectionDetails form with:\n  (a) base64-encoded DER PKCS#8 string\n  (b) PEM string\nRecords warnings emitted, and whether a real expectation run succeeds.\nCleans up RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2 afterwards.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport base64\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport warnings\n\nfrom cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization\nfrom cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.path.expanduser(\"~/Coding/Python/DataQ\"))\n\nACCOUNT = os.environ[\"SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT\"]\nUSER = os.environ[\"SNOWFLAKE_USER\"]\nPASSWORD = os.environ[\"SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD\"]\nDATABASE = \"DATAQ_DB\"\nSCHEMA = \"RETAIL\"\nTABLE = \"ORDERS_HEADER\"\nWAREHOUSE = \"DATAQ_WH\"\nROLE = \"ACCOUNTADMIN\"\n\nkey = rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)\npem = key.private_bytes(\n    encoding=serialization.Encoding.PEM,\n    format=serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,\n    encryption_algorithm=serialization.NoEncryption(),\n).decode()\nder = key.private_bytes(\n    encoding=serialization.Encoding.DER,\n    format=serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,\n    encryption_algorithm=serialization.NoEncryption(),\n)\npub_b64 = base64.b64encode(\n    key.public_key().public_bytes(\n        encoding=serialization.Encoding.DER,\n        format=serialization.PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo,\n    )\n).decode()\n\nimport snowflake.connector  # noqa: E402\n\nadmin = snowflake.connector.connect(\n    account=ACCOUNT, user=USER, password=PASSWORD, role=ROLE, login_timeout=30\n)\nadmin.cursor().execute(f\"ALTER USER {USER} SET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2 = '{pub_b64}'\")\nprint(\"pub key registered\")\n\n\ndef try_form(label: str, private_key_value: str) -> bool:\n    import great_expectations as gx\n    from backend.app.datasources.base import CheckSpec\n    from backend.app.datasources.gx_runner import run_expectations\n\n    context = gx.get_context(mode=\"ephemeral\")\n    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:\n        warnings.simplefilter(\"always\")\n        try:\n            ds = context.data_sources.add_snowflake(\n                name=f\"probe-{label}\",\n                account=ACCOUNT,\n                user=USER,\n                database=DATABASE,\n                schema=SCHEMA,\n                warehouse=WAREHOUSE,\n                role=ROLE,\n                private_key=private_key_value,\n            )\n            asset = ds.add_table_asset(name=TABLE, table_name=TABLE, schema_name=SCHEMA)\n            bd = asset.add_batch_definition_whole_table(name=\"whole_table\")\n            outcome = run_expectations(\n                context,\n                batch_definition=bd,\n                checks=[CheckSpec(\"expect_table_row_count_to_be_between\", {\"min_value\": 0})],\n                name=f\"suite-{label}\",\n            )\n            deprecations = [w for w in caught if issubclass(w.category, DeprecationWarning)]\n            print(f\"[{label}] success={outcome.success} deprecation_warnings={len(deprecations)}\")\n            for w in deprecations:\n                print(f\"    dep-warn: {str(w.message)[:100]}\")\n            return bool(outcome.success)\n        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001\n            print(f\"[{label}] FAILED: {type(exc).__name__}: {str(exc)[:300]}\")\n            return False\n\n\ntry:\n    ok_b64 = try_form(\"b64-der\", base64.standard_b64encode(der).decode())\n    ok_pem = try_form(\"pem\", pem)\n    print(f\"\\nRESULT: b64-der={ok_b64} pem={ok_pem}\")\nfinally:\n    admin.cursor().execute(f\"ALTER USER {USER} UNSET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2\")\n    print(\"cleanup done\")\n    admin.close()\n"

(\n        <Input.TextArea rows={4} autoComplete=\"off\" />\n      ) : (\n        <Input.Password autoComplete=\"off\" />\n      )}\n    </Form.Item>\n  );\n}\n\n/** Optional second secret part (e.g. key-pair passphrase) — rides `composeSecret`.\n * The form's `requiredMark=\"optional\"` renders the (optional) marker.\n * `preserve={false}` drops the value when the field unmounts (auth-mode switch,\n * modal close) so a stale passphrase can never wrap another mode's secret. */\nexport function PassphraseField({ label }: { label: string }) {\n  return (\n    <Form.Item\n      name=\"secretPassphrase\"\n      label={label}\n      preserve={false}\n      extra=\"Only for passphrase-protected keys; leave blank for an unencrypted key.\"\n    >\n      <Input.Password autoComplete=\"off\" />\n    </Form.Item>\n  );\n}"

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/src/components/connections/ReauthModal.tsx",
  "content": "import { App, Form, Modal } from 'antd';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nimport { type Connection, reauthConnection } from '../../api/connections';\nimport { PassphraseField, SecretField } from './ConnectionTypeFields';\nimport { activeAuthOption, composeSecret, CONNECTION_FORM_SPECS } from './connectionFormSpec';\n\n/**\n * Rotate a connection's stored credential. The backend verifies the new\n * credential against the datasource, so a bad value surfaces as an error and the\n * old credential is unaffected. The fields follow the connection's auth mode\n * (from CONNECTION_FORM_SPECS): the shared SecretField/PassphraseField render a\n * multi-line input for PEM keys plus the optional passphrase for key-pair modes,\n * composed the same way as on create (`composeSecret`). `connection === null`\n * means the modal is closed.\n */\nexport function ReauthModal({\n  connection,\n  onClose,\n  onDone,\n}: {\n  connection: Connection | null;\n  onClose: () => void;\n  /** Called after a successful rotation (so the list can refresh `has_secret`). */\n  onDone: () => void;\n}) {\n  const { message } = App.useApp();\n  const [form] = Form.useForm<{ secret: string; secretPassphrase?: string }>();\n  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);\n\n  const auth = connection ? activeAuthOption(connection.type, connection.config) : undefined;\n  const secretLabel =\n    auth?.secretLabel ??\n    (connection && CONNECTION_FORM_SPECS[connection.type].secretLabel) ??\n    'Credential';\n\n  // Values must not survive a close — a passphrase typed for one connection\n  // (then cancelled) must never ride into another connection's rotation.\n  const close = () => {\n    form.resetFields();\n    onClose();\n  };\n\n  const onOk = async () => {\n    if (!connection) return;\n    // antd's Modal `onOk` doesn't catch a rejected handler, so guard the\n    // validation rejection here (errors render inline) rather than letting it\n    // escape as an unhandled promise rejection.\n    let secret: string;\n    let secretPassphrase: string | undefined;\n    try {\n      ({ secret, secretPassphrase } = await form.validateFields());\n    } catch {\n      return;\n    }\n    setSubmitting(true);\n    try {\n      await reauthConnection(\n        connection.id,\n        composeSecret(secret, auth?.passphraseLabel ? secretPassphrase : undefined),\n      );\n      message.success(`${connection.name}: credential rotated`);\n      form.resetFields();\n      onDone();\n    } catch (err) {\n      message.error(`Re-auth failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);\n    } finally {\n      setSubmitting(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <Modal\n      title={connection ? `Re-authenticate “${connection.name}”` : 'Re-authenticate'}\n      open={connection !== null}\n      onOk={onOk}\n      onCancel={close}\n      confirmLoading={submitting}\n      okText=\"Rotate credential\"\n      destroyOnHidden\n    >\n      <Form form={form} layout=\"vertical\" requiredMark=\"optional\">\n        <SecretField\n          label={`New: ${secretLabel}`}\n          multiline={auth?.multilineSecret}\n          extra=\"Rotates the stored credential and verifies it against the datasource.\"\n        />\n        {auth?.passphraseLabel && <PassphraseField label={auth.passphraseLabel} />}\n      </Form>\n    </Modal>\n  );\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';\n\nimport {\n  activeAuthOption,\n  composeSecret,\n} from '../../src/components/connections/connectionFormSpec';\n\ndescribe('composeSecret', () => {\n  it('wraps the secret and passphrase into the combined JSON payload', () => {\n    expect(composeSecret('PEM', 'pp')).toBe(JSON.stringify({ private_key: 'PEM', passphrase: 'pp' }));\n  });\n\n  it('returns the bare secret when the passphrase is missing or empty', () => {\n    expect(composeSecret('PEM')).toBe('PEM');\n    expect(composeSecret('PEM', '')).toBe('PEM');\n  });\n\n  it('treats a whitespace-only passphrase as blank (stray keystroke, not a passphrase)', () => {\n    expect(composeSecret('PEM', '  ')).toBe('PEM');\n  });\n});\n\ndescribe('activeAuthOption', () => {\n  it('resolves the configured auth mode', () => {\n    expect(activeAuthOption('snowflake', { auth_type: 'key_pair' })?.value).toBe('key_pair');\n  });\n\n  it('falls back to the default (first) mode when config carries no auth_type', () => {\n    expect(activeAuthOption('snowflake', {})?.value).toBe('password');\n    expect(activeAuthOption('snowflake', undefined)?.value).toBe('password');\n  });\n\n  it('is undefined for single-secret types', () => {\n    expect(activeAuthOption('s3', {})).toBeUndefined();\n  });\n});\n"
}

All finders are in. The tracer's four candidates share one root: the role requirement fires **late and opaquely** (test-connection passes, then every suite run fails reasonlessly). The clean fix it names — enforce `role` for `key_pair` in `SnowflakeConfig` itself — is better than my run-time guard: the error then surfaces at create/edit/test time with the explicit message, uniformly. Since GX's requirement makes a role-less key-pair connection structurally unable to run suites, making it unrepresentable is the right depth. Implementing:

def test_engine_args_snowflake_key_pair_threads_private_key() -> None:
    from types import SimpleNamespace

    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa

    from backend.app.services.profile_service import _engine_args

    pem = (
        rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)
        .private_bytes(
            encoding=serialization.Encoding.PEM,
            format=serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,
            encryption_algorithm=serialization.NoEncryption(),
        )
        .decode()
    )
    conn = SimpleNamespace(
        type="snowflake",
        config={
            "account": "ab1",
            "user": "u",
            "database": "d",
            "schema": "s",
            "warehouse": "wh",
            "auth_type": "key_pair",
        },
    )
    url, connect_args = _engine_args(conn, pem)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    assert isinstance(connect_args.get("private_key"), bytes)  # DER key threaded in
    assert "u:" not in url  # no password in the DSN

"""Flow A — load to warehouse (Snowflake). §3a.

Scheduled load (the schedule-trigger modality): reads each Snowflake-bound feed from
the ADLS landing zone and overwrites the target table. Pure ETL — no quality-tool
coupling; DataQ discovers these runs by polling the Airflow REST API. Offset to run
AFTER the file-creation Jobs (§2a).

Required env (set on the Airflow Container App, key-based):
  AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING        ADLS read
  SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT/USER/PASSWORD/WAREHOUSE/DATABASE[/SCHEMA/ROLE]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pendulum
from _harness import load_to_snowflake, read_feed
from airflow import DAG
from airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator
from dataq_airflow_callback import on_dataq_failure, on_dataq_success

# Snowflake-bound feeds (route map §2): subdir under the landing zone -> table name.
# All land as CSV (COPY-INTO-friendly in §2).
# Modality split (avoid double-loads): orders_header -> ADF event pipeline;
# customers -> ADF *timer* pipeline; payments -> Airflow *event* (file-sensor) DAG.
# Airflow's schedule modality owns everything else, including the extended domain.

    "order_lines",
    "refunds",
    "returns",
    "products",
    "settlements",
    "purchase_orders",
    "order_fulfillment",
    "discounts",
    "cancellations",
]


def _load(feed: str, **_: object) -> None:
    df = read_feed(f"snowflake/{feed}", "csv")

  "content": "\"\"\"#587 — load the PERF-tier tables into DATAQ_DB.PERF (separate from Flow A's RETAIL).\n\nORDER_LINES (~1.2M rows) is the scale target; ORDERS_HEADER (~400K, has order_ts)\nis the freshness-monitor target. write_pandas, auto-create, overwrite — same load\nmechanism as the harness Flow-A DAG.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport time\n\nimport pandas as pd\nimport snowflake.connector\nfrom snowflake.connector.pandas_tools import write_pandas\n\nBASE = (\n    \"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-arijit-Coding-Python-DataQ/\"\n    \"a9be1a77-8cac-4d65-b95c-94daac919ec8/scratchpad/perf-data/snowflake\"\n)\n\nconn = snowflake.connector.connect(\n    account=os.environ[\"SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT\"],\n    user=os.environ[\"SNOWFLAKE_USER\"],\n    password=os.environ[\"SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD\"],\n    warehouse=\"DATAQ_WH\",\n    database=\"DATAQ_DB\",\n    role=\"ACCOUNTADMIN\",\n    login_timeout=30,\n)\ntry:\n    cur = conn.cursor()\n    cur.execute(\"CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS DATAQ_DB.PERF\")\n    cur.execute(\"USE SCHEMA DATAQ_DB.PERF\")\n    # The DataQ reader role needs to see the new schema (suite runs use it).\n    cur.execute(\"GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA DATAQ_DB.PERF TO ROLE DATAQ_READER\")\n    cur.execute(\"GRANT SELECT ON FUTURE TABLES IN SCHEMA DATAQ_DB.PERF TO ROLE DATAQ_READER\")\n\n    for feed, table in [(\"order_lines\", \"ORDER_LINES\"), (\"orders_header\", \"ORDERS_HEADER\")]:\n        df = pd.read_csv(f\"{BASE}/{feed}/{feed}.csv\")\n        if \"order_ts\" in df.columns:\n            df[\"order_ts\"] = pd.to_datetime(df[\"order_ts\"])\n        df.columns = [c.upper() for c in df.columns]\n        t0 = time.monotonic()\n        _ok, _chunks, rows, _ = write_pandas(\n            conn, df, table, schema=\"PERF\", auto_create_table=True, overwrite=True\n        )\n        print(f\"{table}: {rows} rows loaded in {time.monotonic() - t0:.1f}s\")\n    cur.execute(\"GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA DATAQ_DB.PERF TO ROLE DATAQ_READER\")\n    print(\"grants done\")\nfinally:\n    conn.close()\n"
}

1	"""Full-stack API E2E smoke against a running DataQ stack (no mocks).
2	
3	Drives the **real** HTTP API the way the frontend does — dev-bypass auth, the
4	seeded demo dataset — and asserts the read + authoring paths work end-to-end
5	(HTTP → service → Postgres). Run it after `docker compose up` + the seed:
6	
7	    python -m backend.scripts.e2e_smoke                 # http://localhost:8000
8	    DATAQ_API=http://localhost:8000 python -m backend.scripts.e2e_smoke
9	
10	Against a DEPLOYED stack (real auth), point DATAQ_API at the public frontend
11	(its nginx proxies /api to the internal api) and pass a bearer token:
12	
13	    DATAQ_API=https://<frontend-host> DATAQ_BEARER=$(az account get-access-token \
14	        --resource api://<api-app-id> --query accessToken -o tsv) \
15	        python -m backend.scripts.e2e_smoke
16	
17	Note the authoring round-trip (create suite → check → delete) writes to — and
18	cleans up from — whatever workspace the token can edit; the connection-type
19	assertion expects the demo/harness connection set.
20	
21	What it verifies (exit 0 = all passed):
22	  1. the six seeded connection types are listed (secrets never returned);
23	  2. the demo suites + their checks are retrievable;
24	  3. an authoring round-trip: create suite → add a check → read back → delete;
25	  4. a dry-run *attempt* returns a structured result/error, not a crash
26	     (live connectivity fails-soft without real datasource creds — expected).
27	
28	Live `test()`/runs against real Snowflake/S3/etc. are out of scope (no creds —
29	the documented deferred smoke); this proves the app layer, not the datasources.
30	"""
31	
32	from __future__ import annotations
33	
34	import os
35	import sys
36	import uuid
37	from typing import Any
38	
39	import httpx
40	
41	API = os.environ.get("DATAQ_API", "http://localhost:8000")
42	BASE = f"{API}/api/v1"
43	
44	_passed = 0
45	_failed = 0
46	
47	
48	def check(label: str, ok: bool, detail: str = "") -> None:
49	    global _passed, _failed
50	    mark = "PASS" if ok else "FAIL"
51	    if ok:
52	        _passed += 1
53	    else:
54	        _failed += 1
55	    print(f"[{mark}] {label}" + (f" — {detail}" if detail else ""))
56	
57	
58	def main() -> int:
59	    # Dev-bypass: no bearer needed when AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true + environment=dev.
60	    # Deployed: DATAQ_BEARER carries the Azure AD access token (same token the
61	    # web UI sends), enabling the live-smoke run per the deferred-smoke plan.
62	    bearer = os.environ.get("DATAQ_BEARER")
63	    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {bearer}"} if bearer else {}
64	    client = httpx.Client(base_url=BASE, timeout=30.0, headers=headers)
65	
66	    # 1. Connections — six types present, no secret leaked.
67	    r = client.get("/connections")
68	    conns: list[dict[str, Any]] = r.json() if r.status_code == 200 else []
69	    types = {c["type"] for c in conns}
70	    expected_types = {"snowflake", "s3", "adls_gen2", "unity_catalog", "adf", "airflow"}
71	    check("GET /connections returns 200", r.status_code == 200, f"status={r.status_code}")
72	    check(
73	        "all six connection types seeded",
74	        expected_types.issubset(types),
75	        f"missing={expected_types - types}",
76	    )
77	    check(
78	        "secret is never returned on a connection",
79	        all("secret" not in c and "secret_ref" not in c for c in conns),
80	        "a connection payload leaked a secret field",
81	    )
82	
83	    # 2. Suites + checks retrievable.
84	    r = client.get("/suites")
85	    suites: list[dict[str, Any]] = r.json() if r.status_code == 200 else []
86	    check("GET /suites returns the demo suites", len(suites) >= 3, f"count={len(suites)}")
87	    orders = next((s for s in suites if s["name"] == "Orders quality"), None)
88	    check("'Orders quality' suite present", orders is not None)
89	    if orders is not None:
90	        r = client.get(f"/suites/{orders['id']}/checks")
91	        checks = r.json() if r.status_code == 200 else []
92	        names = {c["name"] for c in checks}
93	        check(
94	            "'Orders quality' has its seeded checks",
95	            {"order_id not null", "amount in range"}.issubset(names),
96	            f"got={sorted(names)}",
97	        )
98	        amount = next((c for c in checks if c["name"] == "amount in range"), None)
99	        check(
100	            "severity thresholds round-trip on a check",
101	            amount is not None and amount["fail_threshold"] == 5,
102	            f"check={amount}",
103	        )
104	
105	    # 3. Authoring round-trip: create suite → add check → read → delete.
106	    # Bind to a *datasource* connection (Snowflake) — suites target datasources,
107	    # not orchestration providers (ADF/Airflow); this also routes the dry-run
108	    # below through the real Snowflake path instead of an unsupported-type 422.
109	    conn_id = next((c["id"] for c in conns if c["type"] == "snowflake"), None)
110	    if conn_id is not None:
111	        name = f"e2e-smoke-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"

# ───────────────────────── column profiler (no persistence) ─────────


class ColumnProfileRequest(ApiModel):
    columns: list[str] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=50)
    top_n: int = Field(default=10, ge=1, le=100, description="Most-frequent values per column")
    # SQL datasources: the target is a table (+ schema; Unity Catalog also catalog).
    table: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255, description="SQL table to profile")
    schema_: str | None = Field(default=None, alias="schema")
    catalog: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255, description="Unity Catalog catalog")
    # Flat-file datasources (ADLS Gen2 / S3): the target is a file path.
    path: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=1024, description="Flat-file path to profile")
    file_format: Literal["csv", "parquet"] | None = None


class TopValue(ApiModel):
    value: Any | None
    count: int


class ColumnProfileRead(ApiModel):
    column: str
    null_count: int
    null_fraction: float
    distinct_count: int | None
    min_value: Any | None
    max_value: Any | None
    top_values: list[TopValue]


class ProfileRead(ApiModel):
    """Profile result. Identity fields are type-specific: SQL datasources fill
    `table` / `schema` (+ `catalog` for Unity Catalog), flat-file datasources fill
    `path` / `file_format`."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)

    row_count: int
    columns: list[ColumnProfileRead]
    table: str | None = None
    schema_: str | None = Field(default=None, serialization_alias="schema")
    catalog: str | None = None
    path: str | None = None
    file_format: str | None = None


@router.post(
    "/suites/{suite_id}/profile",
    response_model=ProfileRead,
    summary="Profile columns of a table/file on the suite's connection (no persistence)",
)
def profile_columns(
    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
    payload: ColumnProfileRequest,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
    secret_store: Annotated[SecretStore, Depends(get_secret_store)],
) -> ProfileRead:
    # sync def → threadpool; the datasource connect + scans/downloads are blocking.
    # Authoring aid → 'edit', same as the dry-run. Connection FK is RESTRICT.
    suite = require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum="edit")
    connection = db.get(Connection, suite.connection_id)
    assert connection is not None
    result = profile.profile_connection(
        connection,
        columns=payload.columns,
        top_n=payload.top_n,
        table=payload.table,
        schema=payload.schema_,
        catalog=payload.catalog,
        path=payload.path,

  "content": "\"\"\"#587 — credits/query-time accounting for the baseline window (last N minutes).\n\nQUERY_HISTORY (information_schema, low lag): per-query execution time on DATAQ_WH.\nWAREHOUSE_METERING_HISTORY: credits for the hour bucket (may still be settling).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nimport snowflake.connector\n\nMINUTES = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 60\n\nconn = snowflake.connector.connect(\n    account=os.environ[\"SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT\"],\n    user=os.environ[\"SNOWFLAKE_USER\"],\n    password=os.environ[\"SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD\"],\n    role=\"ACCOUNTADMIN\",\n    warehouse=\"DATAQ_WH\",\n    login_timeout=30,\n)\ntry:\n    cur = conn.cursor()\n    cur.execute(\n        f\"\"\"\n        SELECT COUNT(*) AS queries,\n               ROUND(SUM(total_elapsed_time)/1000, 1) AS total_elapsed_s,\n               ROUND(SUM(execution_time)/1000, 1) AS execution_s,\n               ROUND(MAX(total_elapsed_time)/1000, 1) AS slowest_s\n        FROM TABLE(INFORMATION_SCHEMA.QUERY_HISTORY(\n            END_TIME_RANGE_START => DATEADD('minute', -{MINUTES}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()),\n            RESULT_LIMIT => 10000))\n        WHERE warehouse_name = 'DATAQ_WH' AND query_type = 'SELECT'\n        \"\"\"\n    )\n    print(\"QUERY_HISTORY (SELECTs on DATAQ_WH, last %d min):\" % MINUTES, cur.fetchone())\n    cur.execute(\n        f\"\"\"\n        SELECT start_time, credits_used, credits_used_compute\n        FROM TABLE(INFORMATION_SCHEMA.WAREHOUSE_METERING_HISTORY(\n            DATE_RANGE_START => DATEADD('minute', -{MINUTES + 60}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()),\n            WAREHOUSE_NAME => 'DATAQ_WH'))\n        ORDER BY start_time\n        \"\"\"\n    )\n    print(\"METERING (hour buckets):\")\n    for row in cur.fetchall():\n        print(\"  \", row)\nfinally:\n    conn.close()\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/docs/perf-baseline-snowflake.md",
  "content": "# Snowflake scale baseline (#587) — the G-b pushdown reference datum\n\n> Captured **2026-07-04**, days before the harness Snowflake subscription lapsed\n> (v1.1 W1). This is the **pushdown-path reference** the v1.1 W6 scale-aware\n> execution work ([#595](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/595) —\n> flat-file/UC sampling + OOM guardrails) is compared against: on a SQL-pushdown\n> datasource, DataQ's cost scales with the *warehouse's* ability to aggregate,\n> not with row volume through the worker. The environment is gone (subscription\n> lapse, #588/#590); the numbers survive here.\n\n## Environment\n\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| Datasource | Snowflake Standard (AWS us-west-2), warehouse `DATAQ_WH` (**XSMALL**, auto-suspend) |\n| Data | `DATAQ_DB.PERF.ORDER_LINES` — **1,199,854 rows** (6 cols) · `DATAQ_DB.PERF.ORDERS_HEADER` — **400,000 rows** (11 cols, `ORDER_TS` timestamp) |\n| Data source | harness mock-data generator, new `PERF` volume tier (400K orders → ~1.2M order lines), loaded via `write_pandas` (ORDER_LINES 11.6s, ORDERS_HEADER 8.2s) |\n| App | local docker-compose stack (api + Celery worker + Postgres + Redis) at `v1.0.0` + #602/#603, driven through the real REST API (dev-bypass) — same code path as prod |\n| Access role | `DATAQ_READER` (least-privilege SELECT), password auth |\n\n## Headline numbers\n\n| Measurement | Value |\n|---|---|\n| Test-connection (`SELECT 1`) | 3.7 s |\n| **Suite run, 1.2M-row table** — 6 expectations + 1 volume monitor | **12.2 s** wall (trigger → terminal), `succeeded`, all pass |\n| **Suite run, 400K-row table** — freshness monitor + 2 expectations | **8.1 s** wall, `succeeded` (freshness metric: age 10.6 h) |\n| **Column profiler, 4 columns on 1.2M rows** (row count, nulls, distinct, min/max, top-10) | **2.6 s** |\n| **Worker memory delta during the 1.2M-row run** | **< 50 MB** (idle 1.99 GiB → peak 2.04 GiB, sampled every 2 s) |\n| Snowflake compute, entire session (2 loads + 3 suite runs + profiler + reruns) | 54 SELECTs, **~2.3 s total execution time**, slowest single query **1.0 s** |\n| Credits burned (metering, XSMALL) | **~0.08 credits** across the session's two hour-buckets (0.024 + 0.056) |\n\n## Per-query attribution (slowest, from `QUERY_HISTORY`)\n\nPer-check `duration_ms` stays NULL in v1 by design (see `run_service.py` — per-check\ntiming is a deferred datum), so per-check cost below is attributed from the\nwarehouse's own query history:\n\n| ms | Query (GX-generated / profiler) |\n|---|---|\n| 647 | unexpected-count aggregate (`SUM(CASE …)`) — the uniqueness/row-condition check on 1.2M rows |\n| 484 | profiler batched aggregate: `COUNT(*)`, nulls, `COUNT(DISTINCT)`, min/max on `LINE_ID` |\n| 388 | unexpected-values sample fetch (`LINE_ID` uniqueness) |\n| 213 | profiler top-10 `GROUP BY` on `LINE_ID` (the ~1.2M-distinct worst case) |\n| 26–52 | remaining profiler top-10s (`QTY`, `UNIT_PRICE`, `SKU_ID`) |\n| ≤ 15 | each between/not-null expectation aggregate; monitor scalars (`MAX(ts)`, `COUNT(*)`) are sub-10ms |\n\n## What this means for #595 (W6 scale-aware execution)\n\n- **Pushdown keeps the worker out of the data path**: 1.2M rows cost the worker\n  <50 MB and the wall time is dominated by GX orchestration + connection setup\n  (~10 s of the 12.2 s; actual warehouse compute ≈ 1.5 s). The flat-file/UC\n  runners, which pull data *into* the worker, are the paths that need sampling +\n  OOM guardrails; this table shape (1.2M × 6 cols ≈ 60 MB CSV) is the reference\n  workload to replay there.\n- **The per-run overhead floor matters more than per-check cost** at this scale:\n  each additional expectation added ~15–650 ms of warehouse time against a ~10 s\n  fixed overhead (ephemeral GX context + engine + validation plumbing per run).\n- **Cost of a realistic schedule is negligible on pushdown**: at ~0.01–0.02\n  credits per suite-run session on XSMALL, even a 15-minute schedule is ~1–2\n  credits/day; the auto-suspend window, not the checks, drives spend.\n- Gaps found while measuring (already tracked): per-check `duration_ms` NULL in\n  v1 (deferred by design); `checks_total` cosmetic 0 on the run list\n  ([#571](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/571)); run failure\n  reasons not surfaced ([#605](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/605)).\n\n## Method / reproducibility\n\nGenerator: `python -m mockdata backfill --tier PERF --seed 587 --no-issues`\n(harness repo, ADR 0021 — the `PERF` tier was added for this baseline). Load:\n`write_pandas` into `DATAQ_DB.PERF` (note: pandas `datetime64` needs\n`use_logical_type=True` or timestamps land as epoch `NUMBER` and freshness\nmonitors error with \"not a date/timestamp\"). Measurement scripts drove the real\nAPI: create connection → test → two suites (targets `PERF.ORDER_LINES` /\n`PERF.ORDERS_HEADER`) → checks incl. `monitor:volume` + `monitor:freshness` →\n`POST /suites/{id}/run` → poll to terminal → results; worker memory sampled via\n`docker stats`; credits via `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.WAREHOUSE_METERING_HISTORY`,\nquery timings via `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.QUERY_HISTORY`.\n"
}

```
Auth seam: DataQ-issued API keys / service tokens (REST + MCP) — provider-neutral identity

## Why

Today authentication is **exclusively Azure AD bearer tokens** (delegated/SSO) for both the REST API and `/mcp` — there is no DataQ-native credential. This is the **deepest remaining vendor lock-in** in the system and cuts against ADR [0010](../docs/adr/0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md) / [0013](../docs/adr/0013-marketplace-distribution-and-anti-lock-in.md): the `get_current_user` seam exists, but it has exactly *one* real implementation and the persistence layer is still Azure-shaped (`users.aad_object_id`). A BYOL customer on AWS/GCP (the ADR 0013 scenario) has no Azure AD and literally cannot authenticate.

It also closes the **programmatic-access gap**: headless agents / CI / always-on MCP clients want a long-lived, scoped, revocable secret — not a ~60-min Azure token they must refresh (see ADR [0008](../docs/adr/0008-mcp-server.md), which uses a token-validating `JWTVerifier`, not a client-driven OAuth provider).

## Scope — cross-cutting, NOT MCP-only

This is a **second authenticator behind the existing generic `get_current_user` seam** (ADR 0010), so the **REST API and `/mcp` accept it identically** — never build it for MCP alone. On MCP, fastmcp's `MultiAuth` lets `/mcp` accept *either* a DataQ key *or* an Azure token. Adding a second auth impl is also what finally *exercises* (validates) the seam.

## Recommended shape (phased)

1. **User-scoped PATs first** — a key belongs to a user and inherits their per-suite grants → **zero new authz model** (reuse the view/edit/admin ladder; optionally down-scope a key to read-only for MCP read tools / dashboards). ~80% of the value for a fraction of the change.
2. **Second authenticator behind the seam** — `Authorization: Bearer dq_live_…` → hash lookup → resolve the principal; else fall back to the Azure JWT. Shared by REST + MCP.
3. **Defer standalone service accounts** — they force the bigger move: generalize `users.aad_object_id` into a generic *principal* with pluggable identity bindings, and extend suite *sharing* to non-user principals. Sequence after PATs prove the seam.

## Security bar (credential surface — do not half-build)

- Hash-at-rest (argon2/bcrypt), **show-once** on creation, identifying prefix (`dq_live_…`), expiry defaults, revocation, last-used + audit.
- Hash lives in a **new `api_keys` table** — *not* the credential SecretStore (that's for retrievable connection secrets; a key hash is a verifier secret, never retrievable).
- **Lifecycle tied to the owner**: deactivating a user kills their keys (no SSO-policy backdoor outliving the account).
- Never log the key (only the prefix) — same discipline as the compliance posture (#436).

## Decision record

Direction captured in **ADR 0026** (Proposed) — auth-provider seam: second authenticator + the principal / identity-binding direction. Framed explicitly as discharging the identity-seam lock-in (ADR 0010/0013).

Post-v1, Theme 3 (Admin, access model & identity).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `api_keys` table: hashed-at-rest, show-once plaintext, key prefix, expiry, revocation; lifecycle tied to the owning user
- [ ] PAT accepted identically by REST AND `/mcp` through the `get_current_user` seam (never MCP-only); inherits the owner's per-suite grants
- [ ] 1 workspace-admin + 1 member PAT minted and exercised live (short expiry on the admin one)
- [ ] Creation/revocation logged; docs cover minting + revoking

_(AC added at v1.1 planning, 2026-07-04.)_
```

3	- **Status:** Proposed — **build deferred to post-v1** (timing decision recorded 2026-07-03; see Decision record below)
4	- **Date:** 2026-06-29 (timing decided 2026-07-03)
5	- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
6	- **Related:** ADR [0010](0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md) (the `get_current_user` identity seam — Azure is one impl, not the architecture), [0013](0013-marketplace-distribution-and-anti-lock-in.md) (BYOL / anti-lock-in), [0008](0008-mcp-server.md) (MCP auth via `JWTVerifier` — bring-your-own-token today), [0020](0020-history-and-audit-strategy.md) (audit), compliance posture (#436)
7	- **Issue:** [#461](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/461)
8	
9	> **Stub — Proposed, not yet designed in full.** Captures the direction while it's fresh; to be fleshed out when Theme 3 (access/identity) is picked up post-v1.
10	
11	## Context
12	
13	Authentication today is **exclusively Azure AD bearer tokens** (delegated/SSO) for both the REST API and `/mcp`. There is no DataQ-native credential. Two problems follow:
14	
15	1. **Lock-in.** This is the deepest remaining Azure coupling. The `get_current_user` seam (ADR 0010) exists and service code never reads Entra claims (CLAUDE.md §11), but the seam has exactly *one* real implementation, and the persistence layer is still Azure-shaped (`users.aad_object_id`). A BYOL customer on AWS/GCP (ADR 0013) has no Azure AD and cannot authenticate at all.
16	2. **No programmatic access.** Headless agents, CI, and always-on MCP clients want a long-lived, scoped, revocable secret — not a ~60-min Azure token they must refresh (ADR 0008 uses a token-*validating* `JWTVerifier`, not a client-driven OAuth provider). There is no API-key / PAT / service-token mechanism.
17	
18	## Decision (direction — to be detailed)
19	
20	Introduce a **DataQ-issued credential as a second authenticator behind the existing `get_current_user` seam**, so the **REST API and `/mcp` accept it identically** — explicitly *not* an MCP-only feature. On MCP, fastmcp `MultiAuth` lets `/mcp` accept either a DataQ key or an Azure token. Adding a second real auth impl is also what *exercises* (and thereby validates) the seam ADR 0010 describes.
21	
22	**Phased:**
23	
24	1. **User-scoped PATs first.** A key belongs to a user and inherits that user's per-suite grants → **no new authz model** (reuse the `view < edit < admin < owner` ladder; optionally down-scope a key to read-only — ideal for MCP read tools / dashboards, smallest blast radius). ~80% of the value for a fraction of the change.
25	2. **Service-account principals later.** These force the larger move and should be sequenced after PATs prove the seam: generalize `users.aad_object_id` into a generic **principal** with pluggable identity bindings (Azure AD oid, API key, …), and extend suite **sharing** to non-user principals.
26	
27	**Credential bar (this is a new secret surface — not to be half-built):**
28	
29	- Hash-at-rest (argon2/bcrypt), **show-once** on creation, identifying prefix (`dq_live_…`), expiry defaults, revocation, last-used + audit.
30	- Hashes live in a **new `api_keys` table** — *not* the credential SecretStore (that store is for *retrievable* connection secrets; a key hash is a verifier secret, never retrievable).
31	- **Lifecycle tied to the owner**: deactivating a user kills their keys, so a PAT can't become an SSO-policy backdoor that outlives the account.
32	- Never logged (prefix only) — same discipline as the compliance posture (#436).
33	
34	## Decision record (2026-07-03 — the go-live "now vs post-v1" call)
35	
36	**Deferred to post-v1 (Theme 3).** Rationale: this is a credential surface with an explicit
37	do-not-half-build bar, and v1's actual programmatic needs are covered by interim mechanisms —
38	the Azure CLI is pre-authorized on the API scope (#565: non-interactive
39	`az account get-access-token` bearers for the live-smoke lane and local MCP clients), and
40	`/mcp` accepts the same Azure token as REST (ADR 0008). Rushing a PAT store into go-live week
41	buys little and risks the exact half-build this ADR warns against.
42	
43	**Shape confirmed** (evaluated against alternatives when the timing was decided):
44	
45	- **User-scoped PATs first** — as phased above. Inherits the per-suite ladder, zero new
46	  authz model, revocable per-integration.
47	- **Standalone service accounts later** — the real need is automation that outlives a person
48	  (owner deactivated → their PATs correctly die), but first-class service principals force the
49	  `users.aad_object_id` → generic-principal migration + non-user sharing; sequence after PATs.
50	  Interim escape hatch: a dedicated service user (e.g. `dataq-admin`) owns automation keys.
51	- **HTTP Basic auth — rejected.** DataQ has no password store (identity is delegated to OIDC);
52	  Basic auth would make DataQ a password system (storage/hashing policy, lockout, reset flows,
53	  credential-stuffing surface) for a *worse* credential: one secret per account (revoking one
54	  integration breaks all), no scoping, no expiry, replayed on every request, and routinely
55	  leaked via logs/proxies. A PAT has the same `Authorization`-header ergonomics without any
56	  of that.
57	
58	## Consequences (anticipated)
59	
60	- Discharges the identity-seam lock-in (ADR 0010/0013): Azure AD becomes *one* authenticator behind the seam, not the only one — unblocking BYOL on non-Azure clouds.
61	- Closes the programmatic-access gap for REST automation and headless MCP clients without weakening the per-user authz model (PAT phase).
62	- Adds a credential-management surface (issue/list/revoke UI + API) and an audit obligation.
63	
64	## Open questions (for the full ADR)
65	
66	- Token format + verification cost (hash lookup on every request — caching?).
67	- Scope granularity: read-only vs read-write vs per-suite.
68	- Where service-account principals sit relative to the workspace-admin allowlist.
69	- Migration path for `users.aad_object_id` → generic principal without breaking existing ownership/shares.
70	
```
