1	"""Azure AD bearer-token auth + user upsert.
2	
3	Two operating modes — picked once at import time from settings:
4	
5	- **Real mode** — `AZURE_TENANT_ID` + `AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID` are set.
6	  Tokens are validated by `fastapi-azure-auth`: issuer, audience, signature,
7	  expiry, and the configured scope. The OpenID config is loaded at app
8	  startup via `init_auth()` and refreshed automatically.
9	
10	- **Dev bypass** — all three of:
11	  `ENVIRONMENT=dev`, `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true`, Azure vars empty.
12	  No token required. Resolves every request to a fixed dev user upserted
13	  into the `users` table. Intended for local development against a
14	  Postgres in `docker-compose` without a real Azure tenant.
15	
16	If neither mode is configured, `init_auth` raises at startup — fail-closed.
17	"""
18	
19	from collections.abc import Callable
20	from datetime import UTC, datetime
21	from typing import Annotated, Any
22	
23	from fastapi import Depends, Security
24	from fastapi_azure_auth import SingleTenantAzureAuthorizationCodeBearer
25	from fastapi_azure_auth.user import User as AzureUser
26	from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import insert
27	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
28	
29	from backend.app.core.config import Settings, get_settings
30	from backend.app.core.errors import DataQError
31	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
32	from backend.app.db.models import User
33	from backend.app.db.session import get_db
34	
35	log = get_logger(__name__)
36	
37	DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
38	DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL = "dev-bypass@dataq.local"
39	DEV_BYPASS_DISPLAY_NAME = "Dev Bypass User"
40	
41	
42	def _dev_bypass_allowed(settings: Settings) -> bool:
43	    return (
44	        settings.environment == "dev"
45	        and settings.auth_dev_bypass
46	        and not settings.azure_auth_configured
47	    )
48	
49	
50	def _build_azure_scheme(
51	    settings: Settings,
52	) -> SingleTenantAzureAuthorizationCodeBearer | None:
53	    if not settings.azure_auth_configured:
54	        return None
55	    assert settings.azure_api_client_id is not None
56	    assert settings.azure_tenant_id is not None
57	    assert settings.azure_api_scope_uri is not None
58	    return SingleTenantAzureAuthorizationCodeBearer(
59	        app_client_id=settings.azure_api_client_id,
60	        tenant_id=settings.azure_tenant_id,
61	        scopes={settings.azure_api_scope_uri: settings.azure_api_scope},
62	        allow_guest_users=settings.azure_allow_guest_users,
63	    )
64	
65	
66	_settings = get_settings()
67	azure_scheme: SingleTenantAzureAuthorizationCodeBearer | None = _build_azure_scheme(_settings)
68	
69	
70	def _upsert_user(
71	    db: Session,
72	    *,
73	    aad_object_id: str,
74	    email: str,
75	    display_name: str | None,
76	) -> User:
77	    now = datetime.now(UTC)
78	    stmt = (
79	        insert(User)
80	        .values(
81	            aad_object_id=aad_object_id,
82	            email=email,
83	            display_name=display_name,
84	            last_seen_at=now,
85	        )
86	        .on_conflict_do_update(
87	            index_elements=["aad_object_id"],
88	            set_={
89	                "email": email,
90	                "display_name": display_name,
91	                "last_seen_at": now,
92	                "updated_at": now,
93	            },
94	        )
95	        .returning(User)
96	    )
97	    user = db.execute(stmt).scalar_one()
98	    db.commit()
99	    return user
100	
101	
102	def _extract_claims(azure_user: AzureUser) -> tuple[str, str, str | None]:
103	    claims: dict[str, Any] = azure_user.claims
104	    aad_oid = str(claims["oid"])
105	    email = str(claims.get("preferred_username") or claims.get("email") or claims.get("upn") or "")
106	    display_name_raw = claims.get("name")
107	    display_name = str(display_name_raw) if display_name_raw is not None else None
108	    return aad_oid, email, display_name
109	
110	
111	async def init_auth() -> None:
112	    """Wire app startup: load OIDC config in real mode, or fail-closed.
113	
114	    Called from the FastAPI lifespan.
115	    """
116	    if azure_scheme is not None:
117	        await azure_scheme.openid_config.load_config()
118	        log.info(
119	            "auth_real_mode_ready",
120	            tenant_id=_settings.azure_tenant_id,
121	            client_id=_settings.azure_api_client_id,
122	            scope=_settings.azure_api_scope_uri,
123	        )
124	        return
125	    if _dev_bypass_allowed(_settings):
126	        log.warning(
127	            "auth_dev_bypass_active",
128	            environment=_settings.environment,
129	            note=(
130	                "Every request resolves to a fixed dev user. "
131	                "Do NOT run with this configuration outside local dev."
132	            ),
133	        )
134	        return
135	    raise RuntimeError(
136	        "Auth not configured. Set AZURE_TENANT_ID + AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID, "
137	        "or set ENVIRONMENT=dev with AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true for local dev."
138	    )
139	
140	
141	def _get_current_user_real(
142	    azure_user: Annotated[AzureUser, Security(azure_scheme)],
143	    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
144	) -> User:
145	    aad_oid, email, display_name = _extract_claims(azure_user)
146	    user = _upsert_user(db, aad_object_id=aad_oid, email=email, display_name=display_name)
147	    log.info("auth_user_resolved", mode="real", aad_oid=aad_oid, user_id=str(user.id))
148	    return user
149	
150	
151	def _get_current_user_dev_bypass(
152	    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
153	) -> User:
154	    user = _upsert_user(
155	        db,
156	        aad_object_id=DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID,
157	        email=DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL,
158	        display_name=DEV_BYPASS_DISPLAY_NAME,
159	    )
160	    log.debug("auth_user_resolved", mode="dev_bypass", user_id=str(user.id))
161	    return user
162	
163	
164	def _get_current_user_unconfigured() -> User:
165	    # init_auth will have raised at startup; this is defence-in-depth.
166	    raise DataQError(
167	        code="auth_not_configured",
168	        message="Authentication is not configured for this environment.",
169	        status_code=503,
170	    )
171	
172	
173	get_current_user: Callable[..., User]
174	if azure_scheme is not None:
175	    get_current_user = _get_current_user_real
176	elif _dev_bypass_allowed(_settings):
177	    get_current_user = _get_current_user_dev_bypass
178	else:
179	    get_current_user = _get_current_user_unconfigured
180	
181	
182	def is_workspace_admin(user: User) -> bool:
183	    """True iff the user is in the workspace-admin allowlist (WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS).
184	
185	    Workspace admin is a single config-driven set — the whole-workspace
186	    administrator, distinct from the per-suite view/edit/admin/owner ladder in
187	    `suite_authz`. Matched case-insensitively on the IdP-supplied email, a
188	    generic identity attribute, so no Azure/Entra claim is read here
189	    (ADR 0010/0013, CLAUDE.md §11). Resolves the allowlist via `get_settings()`
190	    (not the import-time `_settings` singleton) so a test can vary it with
191	    `get_settings.cache_clear()`; in a running process settings are read once at
192	    startup (12-factor — change the env and restart).
193	    """
194	    return get_settings().is_admin_email(user.email)
195	
196	
197	def require_workspace_admin(
198	    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
199	) -> User:
200	    """FastAPI dependency gating the /admin endpoints — 403 for a non-admin.
201	
202	    Server-side authz (never a client toggle): a non-admin gets a real 403, which
203	    the frontend renders as the forbidden page.
204	    """
205	    if not is_workspace_admin(current_user):
206	        raise DataQError(
207	            code="workspace_admin_required",
208	            message="This action requires workspace-admin access.",
209	            status_code=403,
210	        )
211	    return current_user

1	"""Auth for the MCP server — validate the *same* Azure AD bearer token as the REST API.
2	
3	MCP clients (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai / Copilot / Cursor) present the same
4	Azure AD access token the web UI uses. We validate it with a fastmcp
5	``JWTVerifier`` configured from the same tenant / audience / scope as
6	``core.auth`` — issuer, signature (Azure JWKS), expiry, and the required API
7	scope. This mirrors the REST validator without depending on fastapi-azure-auth
8	internals (which are Starlette-request-bound and can't verify a raw token).
9	
10	Two modes, picked from settings exactly like ``core.auth``:
11	
12	- **Real mode** (`azure_auth_configured`): the ``JWTVerifier`` above.
13	- **Dev bypass** (`ENVIRONMENT=dev` + `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true`, no Azure vars): no
14	  verifier — every call resolves to the fixed dev user, for local dev only.
15	
16	If neither is configured the server is **not mounted** (fail-closed — the
17	``/mcp`` endpoint never goes live without auth; CLAUDE.md §10 security note).
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	from typing import Any
23	
24	from fastapi_azure_auth.utils import is_guest
25	from fastmcp.server.auth import AuthProvider
26	from fastmcp.server.auth.providers.jwt import JWTVerifier
27	from fastmcp.server.dependencies import get_access_token
28	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
29	
30	from backend.app.core.auth import (
31	    DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID,
32	    DEV_BYPASS_DISPLAY_NAME,
33	    DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL,
34	    _dev_bypass_allowed,
35	    _upsert_user,
36	)
37	from backend.app.core.config import Settings, get_settings
38	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
39	from backend.app.db.models import User
40	
41	log = get_logger(__name__)
42	
43	
44	class McpAuthError(Exception):
45	    """Raised inside a tool when the caller can't be resolved (defence-in-depth)."""
46	
47	
48	def mcp_enabled(settings: Settings | None = None) -> bool:
49	    """Whether ``/mcp`` should be mounted at all — only when auth is resolvable.
50	
51	    Real Azure auth, or the local dev-bypass. Never an unauthenticated mount in a
52	    deployed (prod/staging) environment.
53	    """
54	    s = settings or get_settings()
55	    return s.azure_auth_configured or _dev_bypass_allowed(s)
56	
57	
58	def build_auth_provider(settings: Settings | None = None) -> AuthProvider | None:
59	    """The fastmcp auth provider — a JWTVerifier in real mode, ``None`` in dev bypass.
60	
61	    Returning ``None`` leaves the mounted server unauthenticated; callers must only
62	    mount in that case when ``_dev_bypass_allowed`` is true (see ``mcp_enabled``).
63	    """
64	    s = settings or get_settings()
65	    if not s.azure_auth_configured:
66	        return None
67	    tenant = s.azure_tenant_id
68	    # Single-tenant v2 endpoint — same coordinates fastapi-azure-auth uses.
69	    return JWTVerifier(
70	        jwks_uri=f"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/discovery/v2.0/keys",
71	        issuer=f"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/v2.0",
72	        audience=s.azure_api_client_id,
73	        required_scopes=[s.azure_api_scope],
74	    )
75	
76	
77	def resolve_current_user(session: Session) -> User:
78	    """Resolve the calling user and upsert them — the MCP twin of ``get_current_user``.
79	
80	    In real mode the validated token's claims (set by the ``JWTVerifier``) supply
81	    the AAD object id + email + name, upserted via the shared ``_upsert_user`` so
82	    the ``users`` row is identical to a web-UI login. In dev bypass (no token) the
83	    fixed dev user is used. Reuses ``core.auth`` so claim handling can't drift.
84	    """
85	    token=[REDACTED]()
86	    if token is not None:
87	        claims: dict[str, Any] = token.claims or {}
88	        # Mirror the REST validator's guest policy: reject Azure AD guests (B2B /
89	        # external) unless explicitly allowed, so /mcp can't accept an identity the
90	        # REST API would 403. The JWTVerifier already validated signature / issuer /
91	        # audience / scope; this is the tenant-membership policy on top.
92	        if not get_settings().azure_allow_guest_users and is_guest(claims):
93	            raise McpAuthError("guest users are not permitted")
94	        # `oid` (the stable directory object id) is mandatory, exactly as the REST
95	        # resolver treats it — never fall back to `sub` (a per-app pairwise
96	        # pseudonym), which would key a divergent / duplicate users row.
97	        aad_oid = claims.get("oid")
98	        if aad_oid:
99	            email = str(
100	                claims.get("preferred_username") or claims.get("email") or claims.get("upn") or ""
101	            )
102	            name = claims.get("name")
103	            return _upsert_user(
104	                session,
105	                aad_object_id=str(aad_oid),
106	                email=email,
107	                display_name=str(name) if name is not None else None,
108	            )
109	    if _dev_bypass_allowed(get_settings()):
110	        return _upsert_user(
111	            session,
112	            aad_object_id=DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID,
113	            email=DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL,
114	            display_name=DEV_BYPASS_DISPLAY_NAME,
115	        )
116	    # Auth provider rejects unauthenticated calls before reaching a tool; this is
117	    # defence-in-depth for the (mis)configured case.
118	    raise McpAuthError("could not resolve an authenticated MCP user")
119

> AGENT

All bookkeeping is done (PR #610 in CI — I'll merge on green). Here's the full picture:

## What happened with the Snowflake leg (needs one action from you)

Awkward timing: the W1 plan said the subscription "lapses within days," so earlier today I executed #588 — retired the leg (schedules off, bindings deleted, KV secrets deleted, PAT revoked). Your message corrected the premise, so I **reversed it**: KV secrets recovered from soft-delete, a **fresh 25-day `DATAQ_READER_PAT`** minted and stored, connections renamed back, and live test-connection is green. The rehearsal wasn't wasted — the retirement procedure is now proven and re-runs at real lapse (~07-25) alongside the #590 wind-down; #588 is reopened on W3.

**One piece I can't restore autonomously** (auto-mode blocked both routes — prod DB firewall and adding myself to `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS`): the **4 schedules are still disabled and 4 trigger bindings deleted**. Options: (a) sign in as **dataq-admin** and restore them in the UI (schedules: Orders Header `*/15`, Payments `0 *`, Customers `*/30`, Order Lines `0 */2`; bindings are listed on [#588](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/588)), or (b) tell me to add `royarijit04@outlook.com` to `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` and I'll do it via the API — that addition is **also needed for #461's live admin-PAT minting**, so I'd recommend (b).

## dbt hosting — my recommendation

**dbt Core, executed by the existing harness Airflow** (a `dbt build` DAG), with local `dbt build` for iteration. Rationale: zero new infra or spend; DataQ's Airflow orchestration monitoring observes dbt runs like any pipeline (real input for the dbt-as-OrchestrationProvider seam, ADR 0011); and the artifacts (`manifest.json`/`run_results.json`) become test input for the W6 lineage design (#596). dbt Cloud adds a SaaS dependency for nothing at this scale. The models: staging **views** over `RETAIL` base tables → mart **dynamic tables** (`dbt-snowflake` supports `materialized='dynamic_table'`), giving true multi-hop lineage plus Snowflake-native `OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES` to test against. Filed as [#609](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/609) (W2).

## Iceberg — v2, and a Databricks caveat

**Iceberg v2** is the right pick: Snowflake's Iceberg support is GA for format-version 2, and every engine reads v2; v3 (deletion vectors, row lineage) is too new and unevenly supported. Plan: write a v2 table (parquet) into the harness ADLS with **PyIceberg** from local, then `CREATE EXTERNAL VOLUME` + object-store catalog integration in Snowflake → foreign Iceberg table → DataQ suite against it. **Caveat**: Databricks **Free Edition likely can't mount external ADLS storage** (no storage credentials/external locations) — the spike will verify, and if blocked I'll test the inverse direction (UC-managed Iceberg via UniForm, read from Snowflake through UC's Iceberg REST catalog), which is the more Free-Edition-friendly path. Pulled [#286](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/286) forward from the W7 stretch into W2 with this plan.

## Where the week stands

W1 is 3/6 done and merged today — #194 (encrypted key-pair, live-verified), #195 (GX key-pair migration — turned out to be an outright bugfix, the old path never validated), #587 (scale baseline: 1.2M-row suite in 12.2s, <50MB worker delta, ~0.08 credits — `docs/perf-baseline-snowflake.md`). Next I'm continuing **#461 (PATs phase 1)**, then #583; the dbt and Iceberg work starts after those (they're W2-scheduled, and the window now comfortably allows it).

Create Date: 2026-06-20 00:00:00.000000+00:00

Adds the ``schedules`` table backing the scheduling backend (A7): a cron
expression + IANA timezone per suite that the beat dispatcher
(``worker.tasks.dispatch_due_schedules``) fires on. ``next_run_at`` is the
precomputed next fire (UTC); the dispatcher scans ``enabled, next_run_at`` (hot
path) and only ever parses cron when a schedule actually fires. A schedule is
cascade-deleted with its suite.

Backward-compatible: a brand-new table, no change to existing tables, no data
rewrite, no two-step.
"""

from collections.abc import Sequence

import sqlalchemy as sa
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import UUID

from alembic import op

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/services/api_key_service.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"DataQ-issued personal access tokens (PATs) — ADR 0026 phase 1 (#461).\n\nA PAT is a high-entropy random token (`dq_live_` + 43 url-safe chars,\n~256 bits) shown ONCE at creation. Only its SHA-256 hex digest is stored —\nsufficient hashing for a random machine secret (unlike a human password there\nis nothing to brute-force), and it keeps per-request verification an O(1)\nindexed lookup instead of an argon2/bcrypt stretch per call (GitHub/GitLab use\nthe same scheme for their PATs; rationale recorded in ADR 0026).\n\nThe token authenticates as its owning user through the same `get_current_user`\nseam as Azure AD — REST and `/mcp` identically — inheriting the owner's\nper-suite grants. Keys cascade-delete with the user (lifecycle tied to the\naccount). The plaintext is never logged; log lines carry `key_prefix` only.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport hashlib\nimport secrets\nimport uuid\nfrom datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta\n\nfrom sqlalchemy import select\nfrom sqlalchemy.orm import Session\n\nfrom backend.app.core.errors import DataQError\nfrom backend.app.core.logging import get_logger\nfrom backend.app.db.models import ApiKey, User\n\nlog = get_logger(__name__)\n\nTOKEN_PREFIX = \"dq_live_\"\n# Shown in lists/logs to identify a key without revealing it: `dq_live_` + 4.\n_DISPLAY_PREFIX_LEN = len(TOKEN_PREFIX) + 4\n\nDEFAULT_EXPIRY_DAYS = 90\nMAX_EXPIRY_DAYS = 365\n\n# last_used_at is telemetry, not an audit ledger — throttle writes so a chatty\n# client doesn't turn every request into an UPDATE.\n_LAST_USED_WRITE_INTERVAL = timedelta(seconds=60)\n\n\nclass ApiKeyAuthError(DataQError):\n    \"\"\"The presented token is unknown, revoked, or expired — always a 401.\n\n    One message for every failure mode: distinguishing 'unknown' from\n    'revoked'/'expired' would confirm to a probing caller that a credential\n    exists.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        super().__init__(\n            code=\"invalid_api_key\",\n            message=\"API key is invalid, revoked, or expired.\",\n            status_code=401,\n        )\n\n\nclass ApiKeyNotFoundError(DataQError):\n    def __init__(self, key_id: uuid.UUID) -> None:\n        super().__init__(\n            code=\"api_key_not_found\",\n            message=\"API key not found.\",\n            status_code=404,\n            detail={\"api_key_id\": str(key_id)},\n        )\n\n\ndef _hash(token: str) -> str:\n    return hashlib.sha256(token.encode()).hexdigest()\n\n\ndef create_key(\n    db: Session,\n    user: User,\n    *,\n    name: str,\n    expires_in_days: int = DEFAULT_EXPIRY_DAYS,\n) -> tuple[ApiKey, str]:\n    \"\"\"Mint a PAT for `user`. Returns (row, plaintext) — the ONLY time the\n    plaintext exists server-side; it is never stored or logged.\"\"\"\n    if not 1 <= expires_in_days <= MAX_EXPIRY_DAYS:\n        raise DataQError(\n            code=\"api_key_expiry_invalid\",\n            message=f\"expires_in_days must be between 1 and {MAX_EXPIRY_DAYS}.\",\n            status_code=422,\n        )\n    token = TOKEN_PREFIX + secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    key = ApiKey(\n        id=uuid.uuid4(),\n        user_id=user.id,\n        name=name,\n        key_prefix=token[:_DISPLAY_PREFIX_LEN],\n        key_hash=_hash(token),\n        expires_at=datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=expires_in_days),\n    )\n    db.add(key)\n    db.commit()\n    db.refresh(key)\n    log.info(\n        \"api_key_created\",\n        api_key_id=str(key.id),\n        user_id=str(user.id),\n        key_prefix=key.key_prefix,\n        expires_at=key.expires_at.isoformat(),\n    )\n    return key, token\n\n\ndef list_keys(db: Session, user: User) -> list[ApiKey]:\n    \"\"\"The user's keys, newest first — metadata only (hashes never leave the DB layer).\"\"\"\n    return list(\n        db.execute(\n            select(ApiKey).where(ApiKey.user_id == user.id).order_by(ApiKey.created_at.desc())\n        )\n        .scalars()\n        .all()\n    )\n\n\ndef revoke_key(db: Session, user: User, key_id: uuid.UUID) -> ApiKey:\n    \"\"\"Revoke one of the user's own keys. Idempotent; 404 for another user's key\n    (indistinguishable from nonexistent — no cross-user probing).\"\"\"\n    key = db.execute(\n        select(ApiKey).where(ApiKey.id == key_id, ApiKey.user_id == user.id)\n    ).scalar_one_or_none()\n    if key is None:\n        raise ApiKeyNotFoundError(key_id)\n    if key.revoked_at is None:\n        key.revoked_at = datetime.now(UTC)\n        db.commit()\n        log.info(\n            \"api_key_revoked\",\n            api_key_id=str(key.id),\n            user_id=str(user.id),\n            key_prefix=key.key_prefix,\n        )\n    return key\n\n\ndef resolve_token(db: Session, token: str) -> User:\n    \"\"\"Authenticate a presented PAT → its owning User, or raise ApiKeyAuthError.\n\n    O(1): unique-index lookup on the token's hash. Expiry/revocation checked on\n    the row; `last_used_at` refreshed at most once per interval.\n    \"\"\"\n    key = db.execute(\n        select(ApiKey).where(ApiKey.key_hash == _hash(token))\n    ).scalar_one_or_none()\n    now = datetime.now(UTC)\n    if key is None or key.revoked_at is not None or key.expires_at <= now:\n        # Prefix-only logging — never the token.\n        log.warning(\"api_key_auth_failed\", key_prefix=token[:_DISPLAY_PREFIX_LEN])\n        raise ApiKeyAuthError()\n    user = db.get(User, key.user_id)\n    if user is None:  # cascade should make this unreachable; fail closed anyway\n        log.warning(\"api_key_orphaned\", api_key_id=str(key.id), key_prefix=key.key_prefix)\n        raise ApiKeyAuthError()\n    if key.last_used_at is None or now - key.last_used_at >= _LAST_USED_WRITE_INTERVAL:\n        key.last_used_at = now\n        db.commit()\n    log.info(\n        \"auth_user_resolved\",\n        mode=\"api_key\",\n        api_key_id=str(key.id),\n        user_id=str(user.id),\n    )\n    return user\n"
}

  "old_string": "def _build_azure_scheme(\n    settings: Settings,\n) -> SingleTenantAzureAuthorizationCodeBearer | None:\n    if not settings.azure_auth_configured:\n        return None\n    assert settings.azure_api_client_id is not None\n    assert settings.azure_tenant_id is not None\n    assert settings.azure_api_scope_uri is not None\n    return SingleTenantAzureAuthorizationCodeBearer(\n        app_client_id=settings.azure_api_client_id,\n        tenant_id=settings.azure_tenant_id,\n        scopes={settings.azure_api_scope_uri: settings.azure_api_scope},\n        allow_guest_users=settings.azure_allow_guest_users,\n    )",
  "new_string": "def _build_azure_scheme(\n    settings: Settings,\n) -> SingleTenantAzureAuthorizationCodeBearer | None:\n    if not settings.azure_auth_configured:\n        return None\n    assert settings.azure_api_client_id is not None\n    assert settings.azure_tenant_id is not None\n    assert settings.azure_api_scope_uri is not None\n    return SingleTenantAzureAuthorizationCodeBearer(\n        app_client_id=settings.azure_api_client_id,\n        tenant_id=settings.azure_tenant_id,\n        scopes={settings.azure_api_scope_uri: settings.azure_api_scope},\n        allow_guest_users=settings.azure_allow_guest_users,\n        # auto_error=False so a failed Azure validation yields None instead of\n        # raising — get_current_user then rejects with the standard error\n        # envelope. Required for the PAT path (ADR 0026): a `dq_live_…` bearer\n        # is not a JWT and must not be force-rejected by the Azure scheme.\n        auto_error=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef _bearer_token(request: Request) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The raw bearer token from the Authorization header, if any.\"\"\"\n    header = request.headers.get(\"Authorization\", \"\")\n    scheme, _, token = header.partition(\" \")\n    if scheme.lower() == \"bearer\" and token.strip():\n        return token.strip()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _pat_token(request: Request) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The bearer token when it is a DataQ PAT (by prefix), else None.\"\"\"\n    token = _bearer_token(request)\n    if token is not None and token.startswith(api_key_service.TOKEN_PREFIX):\n        return token\n    return None"

  "new_string": "def _get_current_user_real(\n    request: Request,\n    azure_user: Annotated[AzureUser | None, Security(azure_scheme)],\n    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],\n) -> User:\n    # DataQ PAT first, by prefix (ADR 0026 — second authenticator behind the\n    # seam): a `dq_live_…` bearer is never a valid JWT, so the branches are\n    # disjoint. api_key_service raises the uniform 401 on any bad key.\n    pat = _pat_token(request)\n    if pat is not None:\n        return api_key_service.resolve_token(db, pat)\n    if azure_user is None:\n        # auto_error=False left rejection to us: no/invalid Azure token.\n        raise DataQError(\n            code=\"unauthenticated\",\n            message=\"Not authenticated: a valid Azure AD token or DataQ API key is required.\",\n            status_code=401,\n        )\n    aad_oid, email, display_name = _extract_claims(azure_user)\n    user = _upsert_user(db, aad_object_id=aad_oid, email=email, display_name=display_name)\n    log.info(\"auth_user_resolved\", mode=\"real\", aad_oid=aad_oid, user_id=str(user.id))\n    return user\n\n\ndef _get_current_user_dev_bypass(\n    request: Request,\n    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],\n) -> User:\n    # PATs resolve in dev bypass too (same seam order as real mode), so the\n    # local stack can exercise the full PAT lifecycle without Azure.\n    pat = _pat_token(request)\n    if pat is not None:\n        return api_key_service.resolve_token(db, pat)\n    user = _upsert_user(\n        db,\n        aad_object_id=DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID,\n        email=DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL,\n        display_name=DEV_BYPASS_DISPLAY_NAME,\n    )\n    log.debug(\"auth_user_resolved\", mode=\"dev_bypass\", user_id=str(user.id))\n    return user"

  "old_string": "def build_auth_provider(settings: Settings | None = None) -> AuthProvider | None:\n    \"\"\"The fastmcp auth provider — a JWTVerifier in real mode, ``None`` in dev bypass.\n\n    Returning ``None`` leaves the mounted server unauthenticated; callers must only\n    mount in that case when ``_dev_bypass_allowed`` is true (see ``mcp_enabled``).\n    \"\"\"\n    s = settings or get_settings()\n    if not s.azure_auth_configured:\n        return None\n    tenant = s.azure_tenant_id\n    # Single-tenant v2 endpoint — same coordinates fastapi-azure-auth uses.\n    return JWTVerifier(\n        jwks_uri=f\"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/discovery/v2.0/keys\",\n        issuer=f\"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/v2.0\",\n        audience=s.azure_api_client_id,\n        required_scopes=[s.azure_api_scope],\n    )",
  "new_string": "class _PatOrJwtVerifier(TokenVerifier):\n    \"\"\"Composite verifier: DataQ PAT by prefix, else the Azure ``JWTVerifier``.\n\n    The branches are disjoint (a ``dq_live_…`` bearer is never a valid JWT).\n    A bad PAT returns ``None`` — fastmcp turns that into the standard 401 —\n    and is logged prefix-only inside ``api_key_service``.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, jwt_verifier: JWTVerifier) -> None:\n        super().__init__()\n        self._jwt = jwt_verifier\n\n    async def verify_token(self, token: str) -> AccessToken | None:\n        if not token.startswith(api_key_service.TOKEN_PREFIX):\n            return await self._jwt.verify_token(token)\n        from backend.app.db.session import SessionLocal\n\n        session = SessionLocal()\n        try:\n            user = api_key_service.resolve_token(session, token)\n        except DataQError:\n            return None\n        finally:\n            session.close()\n        return AccessToken(\n            token=token,\n            client_id=\"dataq-pat\",\n            scopes=[],\n            expires_at=None,\n            claims={PAT_USER_CLAIM: str(user.id)},\n        )\n\n\ndef build_auth_provider(settings: Settings | None = None) -> AuthProvider | None:\n    \"\"\"The fastmcp auth provider — PAT-or-Azure-JWT in real mode, ``None`` in dev bypass.\n\n    Returning ``None`` leaves the mounted server unauthenticated; callers must only\n    mount in that case when ``_dev_bypass_allowed`` is true (see ``mcp_enabled``).\n    \"\"\"\n    s = settings or get_settings()\n    if not s.azure_auth_configured:\n        return None\n    tenant = s.azure_tenant_id\n    # Single-tenant v2 endpoint — same coordinates fastapi-azure-auth uses.\n    jwt = JWTVerifier(\n        jwks_uri=f\"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/discovery/v2.0/keys\",\n        issuer=f\"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/v2.0\",\n        audience=s.azure_api_client_id,\n        required_scopes=[s.azure_api_scope],\n    )\n    return _PatOrJwtVerifier(jwt)"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/api/v1/api_keys.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Personal access tokens (PATs) — mint / list / revoke (ADR 0026 phase 1, #461).\n\nUser-scoped: every route operates on the caller's own keys. The plaintext token\nappears exactly once, in the creation response; list/read return metadata only\n(prefix, expiry, revocation, last-used). Revocation is a soft mark\n(`revoked_at`), keeping the row for audit.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport uuid\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom typing import Annotated\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, status\nfrom pydantic import ConfigDict, Field\nfrom sqlalchemy.orm import Session\n\nfrom backend.app.api.v1._base import ApiModel\nfrom backend.app.core.auth import get_current_user\nfrom backend.app.db.models import User\nfrom backend.app.db.session import get_db\nfrom backend.app.services import api_key_service as svc\n\nrouter = APIRouter(tags=[\"auth\"])\n\n\nclass ApiKeyCreate(ApiModel):\n    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=128, description=\"Label, e.g. 'ci-smoke'\")\n    expires_in_days: int = Field(\n        default=svc.DEFAULT_EXPIRY_DAYS,\n        ge=1,\n        le=svc.MAX_EXPIRY_DAYS,\n        description=\"Days until the key expires (no non-expiring keys)\",\n    )\n\n\nclass ApiKeyRead(ApiModel):\n    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)\n\n    id: uuid.UUID\n    name: str\n    key_prefix: str\n    created_at: datetime\n    expires_at: datetime\n    revoked_at: datetime | None\n    last_used_at: datetime | None\n\n\nclass ApiKeyCreated(ApiKeyRead):\n    \"\"\"Creation response — the ONLY place the plaintext token ever appears.\"\"\"\n\n    token: str = Field(description=\"The API key. Shown once; store it now.\")\n\n\n@router.post(\n    \"/me/api-keys\",\n    response_model=ApiKeyCreated,\n    status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,\n    summary=\"Mint an API key (personal access token) — plaintext shown once\",\n)\ndef create_api_key(\n    payload: ApiKeyCreate,\n    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],\n    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],\n) -> ApiKeyCreated:\n    \"\"\"Mint a PAT that authenticates as you (`Authorization: Bearer dq_live_…`)\n    on the REST API and `/mcp` alike, inheriting your per-suite access.\"\"\"\n    key, token = svc.create_key(\n        db, current_user, name=payload.name, expires_in_days=payload.expires_in_days\n    )\n    resp = ApiKeyCreated.model_validate(key, update={\"token\": token})\n    return resp\n\n\n@router.get(\n    \"/me/api-keys\",\n    response_model=list[ApiKeyRead],\n    summary=\"List your API keys (metadata only — never the token)\",\n)\ndef list_api_keys(\n    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],\n    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],\n) -> list[ApiKeyRead]:\n    return [ApiKeyRead.model_validate(k) for k in svc.list_keys(db, current_user)]\n\n\n@router.delete(\n    \"/me/api-keys/{key_id}\",\n    status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT,\n    summary=\"Revoke one of your API keys\",\n)\ndef revoke_api_key(\n    key_id: uuid.UUID,\n    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],\n    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Revocation is immediate (the key stops authenticating) and idempotent.\n    Another user's key 404s — indistinguishable from a nonexistent one.\"\"\"\n    svc.revoke_key(db, current_user, key_id)\n"
}

"""/me endpoint tests — focus on the `is_workspace_admin` flag the Admin nav
gates on. Auth is dev-bypass (conftest); WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS toggles whether
the caller is an admin. Skips without TEST_DATABASE_URL.
"""

from collections.abc import Iterator
from typing import Any

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from backend.app.core.auth import DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL
from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
from backend.app.db.session import get_db
from backend.app.main import app


@pytest.fixture
def client(db_session: Any) -> Iterator[TestClient]:
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: db_session
    try:
        yield TestClient(app)
    finally:
        app.dependency_overrides.clear()


def test_me_flags_non_admin_by_default(client: TestClient) -> None:
    get_settings.cache_clear()
    body = client.get("/api/v1/me").json()
    assert body["email"] == DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL
    assert body["is_workspace_admin"] is False


def test_me_flags_admin_when_allowlisted(
    client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS", f"someone@else.io,{DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL}")
    get_settings.cache_clear()
    body = client.get("/api/v1/me").json()
    assert body["is_workspace_admin"] is True

## Your dbt question: separate orchestration layer, or clubbed with Airflow?

**Clubbed with Airflow — and that's the right thing for us.** In DataQ's model, an orchestration provider is whatever engine *executes and reports* pipeline runs. If dbt runs as an Airflow DAG (a `dbt build` task, or Cosmos rendering each model as a task), then from DataQ's point of view there is no dbt at all — there's an Airflow DAG named `dbt_build_retail` whose runs land in `pipeline_runs` via the existing Airflow provider, complete with the HMAC callback, trigger-on-success bindings, and 10-min polling fallback. Zero new code; we exercise the orchestration seam against a realistic ELT workload for free.

The **dbt-as-`OrchestrationProvider`** seam (ADR 0011) is for a different situation: dbt running *outside* any engine DataQ observes — dbt Cloud jobs, or standalone `dbt` cron. Then DataQ would need a dbt provider implementation (polling the dbt Cloud API or reading `run_results.json`) to see runs at all. We don't need that while Airflow hosts it — but the artifacts we'll capture (`manifest.json`, `run_results.json`) are exactly what a future dbt provider or the OpenLineage work (#596) would consume, so hosting in Airflow now doesn't foreclose promoting dbt to a first-class provider later.

Two orthogonal things dbt gives us regardless of hosting: **model-level lineage** (manifest DAG + Snowflake `OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES` from the views/dynamic tables) — the #596 test bed — and, if we ever want task-per-model observability inside DataQ, Cosmos gives that within the Airflow provider too.

**Where things stand:** W1 is 3/6 (#194/#195/#587 merged); #461 PATs is mid-build — migration, model, service, REST+MCP seam wiring, and the service test battery are written; next are the API/auth/MCP tests, docs, ADR 0026 update, then PR + review + the live minting (admin PAT as dataq-admin — your az login came at the right time). #583, then the dbt project (#609) and Iceberg spike (#286) follow.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about dbt Cloud's Developer plan, free tier, API access, webhooks, and 2026 pricing:

## Developer Plan (Free Tier)

The Developer plan is dbt Cloud's free tier - for individual use, dbt Cloud is free. The Developer tier is free and includes 1 seat, 3,000 models/month, and a 14-day trial of Starter features. The Developer tier does not include job scheduling, CI/CD integration, or API access.

## API Access and Webhooks

Accounts on the Starter, Enterprise, and Enterprise+ plans can query the dbt APIs. This means API access is **not** available on the free Developer plan. For webhooks, refer to Webhooks for your jobs. (Webhooks appear to be available on paid plans as well.)

## Paid Plans and 2026 Pricing

Starter is $100 per user per month and includes 15,000 successful models built per month, 5,000 queried metrics per month, and one project. The Team plan includes unlimited projects, job scheduling (cron-based), CI/CD integration (run dbt tests on pull requests), API access for programmatic interaction, and hosted documentation.

For Enterprise plans, public pricing is available for Developer and Starter, while Enterprise and Enterprise+ are contract-based.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about dbt Projects on Snowflake with native dbt Core execution and workspace scheduling:

## Running dbt Core Natively on Snowflake

Snowflake's dbt Projects feature allows you to run dbt Core projects natively inside Snowflake. When executed, dbt Core runs within Snowflake's compute layer, with SQL compiled, the DAG resolved, and queries dispatched against your data — all without leaving Snowflake's security perimeter.

## Workspaces for Development

Workspaces in the Snowflake web interface are a Git-connected web IDE where you can visualize, test, run, and scaffold one or many dbt projects, link them to a Snowflake dbt project object to create/update it, and edit other Snowflake code in one place.

## Scheduling dbt Project Execution

You can use Snowflake tasks to schedule execution of a dbt project object with the EXECUTE DBT PROJECT command. From a workspace, you can quickly create and schedule a user-managed task to execute a connected dbt project object. Frequency options range from Hourly to Monthly with an at qualifier, or you can choose Custom and enter a Cron expression.

## Current Status

Snowflake went GA with dbt Projects in November 2025, making this feature generally available for production use. The feature consolidates development, testing, deployment, scheduling, and monitoring all within the Snowflake platform.

"""/me endpoint tests — focus on the `is_workspace_admin` flag the Admin nav
gates on. Auth is dev-bypass (conftest); WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS toggles whether
the caller is an admin. Skips without TEST_DATABASE_URL.
"""

from collections.abc import Iterator
from typing import Any

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from backend.app.core.auth import DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL
from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
from backend.app.db.session import get_db
from backend.app.main import app


@pytest.fixture
def client(db_session: Any) -> Iterator[TestClient]:
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: db_session
    try:
        yield TestClient(app)
    finally:
        app.dependency_overrides.clear()


def test_me_flags_non_admin_by_default(client: TestClient) -> None:
    get_settings.cache_clear()
    body = client.get("/api/v1/me").json()
    assert body["email"] == DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL
    assert body["is_workspace_admin"] is False


def test_me_flags_admin_when_allowlisted(
    client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS", f"someone@else.io,{DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL}")
    get_settings.cache_clear()
    body = client.get("/api/v1/me").json()
    assert body["is_workspace_admin"] is True
```

1	"""Bearer-token auth (Azure AD or DataQ PAT) + user upsert.
2	
3	Two operating modes — picked once at import time from settings:
4	
5	- **Real mode** — `AZURE_TENANT_ID` + `AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID` are set.
6	  Two authenticators behind the one `get_current_user` seam (ADR 0026):
7	  a **DataQ PAT** (`Authorization: Bearer dq_live_…` → hashed lookup in
8	  `api_keys`, resolving to the owning user) is tried first by prefix;
9	  anything else is an **Azure AD token** validated by `fastapi-azure-auth`
10	  (issuer, audience, signature, expiry, scope — OpenID config loaded at app
11	  startup via `init_auth()` and refreshed automatically).
12	
13	- **Dev bypass** — all three of:
14	  `ENVIRONMENT=dev`, `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true`, Azure vars empty.
15	  No token required. Resolves every request to a fixed dev user upserted
16	  into the `users` table. Intended for local development against a
17	  Postgres in `docker-compose` without a real Azure tenant. (PATs still
18	  resolve in dev bypass when presented — the same seam order.)
19	
20	If neither mode is configured, `init_auth` raises at startup — fail-closed.
21	"""
22	
23	from collections.abc import Callable
24	from datetime import UTC, datetime
25	from typing import Annotated, Any
26	
27	from fastapi import Depends, Request, Security
28	from fastapi_azure_auth import SingleTenantAzureAuthorizationCodeBearer
29	from fastapi_azure_auth.user import User as AzureUser
30	from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import insert
31	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
32	
33	from backend.app.core.config import Settings, get_settings
34	from backend.app.core.errors import DataQError
35	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
36	from backend.app.db.models import User
37	from backend.app.db.session import get_db
38	from backend.app.services import api_key_service
39	
40	log = get_logger(__name__)
41	
42	DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
43	DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL = "dev-bypass@dataq.local"
44	DEV_BYPASS_DISPLAY_NAME = "Dev Bypass User"
45	
46	
47	def _dev_bypass_allowed(settings: Settings) -> bool:
48	    return (
49	        settings.environment == "dev"
50	        and settings.auth_dev_bypass
51	        and not settings.azure_auth_configured
52	    )
53	
54	
55	def _build_azure_scheme(
56	    settings: Settings,
57	) -> SingleTenantAzureAuthorizationCodeBearer | None:
58	    if not settings.azure_auth_configured:
59	        return None
60	    assert settings.azure_api_client_id is not None
61	    assert settings.azure_tenant_id is not None
62	    assert settings.azure_api_scope_uri is not None
63	    return SingleTenantAzureAuthorizationCodeBearer(
64	        app_client_id=settings.azure_api_client_id,
65	        tenant_id=settings.azure_tenant_id,
66	        scopes={settings.azure_api_scope_uri: settings.azure_api_scope},
67	        allow_guest_users=settings.azure_allow_guest_users,
68	        # auto_error=False so a failed Azure validation yields None instead of
69	        # raising — get_current_user then rejects with the standard error
70	        # envelope. Required for the PAT path (ADR 0026): a `dq_live_…` bearer
71	        # is not a JWT and must not be force-rejected by the Azure scheme.
72	        auto_error=False,
73	    )
74	
75	
76	def _bearer_token(request: Request) -> str | None:
77	    """The raw bearer token from the Authorization header, if any."""
78	    header = request.headers.get("Authorization", "")
79	    scheme, _, token = header.partition(" ")
80	    if scheme.lower() == "bearer" and token.strip():
81	        return token.strip()
82	    return None
83	
84	
85	def _pat_token(request: Request) -> str | None:
86	    """The bearer token when it is a DataQ PAT (by prefix), else None."""
87	    token = _bearer_token(request)
88	    if token is not None and token.startswith(api_key_service.TOKEN_PREFIX):
89	        return token
90	    return None
91	
92	
93	_settings = get_settings()
94	azure_scheme: SingleTenantAzureAuthorizationCodeBearer | None = _build_azure_scheme(_settings)
95	
96	
97	def _upsert_user(
98	    db: Session,
99	    *,
100	    aad_object_id: str,
101	    email: str,
102	    display_name: str | None,
103	) -> User:
104	    now = datetime.now(UTC)
105	    stmt = (
106	        insert(User)
107	        .values(
108	            aad_object_id=aad_object_id,
109	            email=email,
110	            display_name=display_name,
111	            last_seen_at=now,
112	        )
113	        .on_conflict_do_update(
114	            index_elements=["aad_object_id"],
115	            set_={
116	                "email": email,
117	                "display_name": display_name,
118	                "last_seen_at": now,
119	                "updated_at": now,
120	            },
121	        )
122	        .returning(User)
123	    )
124	    user = db.execute(stmt).scalar_one()
125	    db.commit()
126	    return user
127	
128	
129	def _extract_claims(azure_user: AzureUser) -> tuple[str, str, str | None]:
130	    claims: dict[str, Any] = azure_user.claims
131	    aad_oid = str(claims["oid"])
132	    email = str(claims.get("preferred_username") or claims.get("email") or claims.get("upn") or "")
133	    display_name_raw = claims.get("name")
134	    display_name = str(display_name_raw) if display_name_raw is not None else None
135	    return aad_oid, email, display_name
136	
137	
138	async def init_auth() -> None:
139	    """Wire app startup: load OIDC config in real mode, or fail-closed.
140	
141	    Called from the FastAPI lifespan.
142	    """
143	    if azure_scheme is not None:
144	        await azure_scheme.openid_config.load_config()
145	        log.info(
146	            "auth_real_mode_ready",
147	            tenant_id=_settings.azure_tenant_id,
148	            client_id=_settings.azure_api_client_id,
149	            scope=_settings.azure_api_scope_uri,
150	        )
151	        return
152	    if _dev_bypass_allowed(_settings):
153	        log.warning(
154	            "auth_dev_bypass_active",
155	            environment=_settings.environment,
156	            note=(
157	                "Every request resolves to a fixed dev user. "
158	                "Do NOT run with this configuration outside local dev."
159	            ),
160	        )
161	        return
162	    raise RuntimeError(
163	        "Auth not configured. Set AZURE_TENANT_ID + AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID, "
164	        "or set ENVIRONMENT=dev with AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true for local dev."
165	    )
166	
167	
168	def _get_current_user_real(
169	    request: Request,
170	    azure_user: Annotated[AzureUser | None, Security(azure_scheme)],
171	    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
172	) -> User:
173	    # DataQ PAT first, by prefix (ADR 0026 — second authenticator behind the
174	    # seam): a `dq_live_…` bearer is never a valid JWT, so the branches are
175	    # disjoint. api_key_service raises the uniform 401 on any bad key.
176	    pat = _pat_token(request)
177	    if pat is not None:
178	        return api_key_service.resolve_token(db, pat)
179	    if azure_user is None:
180	        # auto_error=False left rejection to us: no/invalid Azure token.
181	        raise DataQError(
182	            code="unauthenticated",
183	            message="Not authenticated: a valid Azure AD token or DataQ API key is required.",
184	            status_code=401,
185	        )
186	    aad_oid, email, display_name = _extract_claims(azure_user)
187	    user = _upsert_user(db, aad_object_id=aad_oid, email=email, display_name=display_name)
188	    log.info("auth_user_resolved", mode="real", aad_oid=aad_oid, user_id=str(user.id))
189	    return user
190	
191	
192	def _get_current_user_dev_bypass(
193	    request: Request,
194	    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
195	) -> User:
196	    # PATs resolve in dev bypass too (same seam order as real mode), so the
197	    # local stack can exercise the full PAT lifecycle without Azure.
198	    pat = _pat_token(request)
199	    if pat is not None:

205	        display_name=DEV_BYPASS_DISPLAY_NAME,

229	def is_workspace_admin(user: User) -> bool:
230	    """True iff the user is in the workspace-admin allowlist (WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS).
231	
232	    Workspace admin is a single config-driven set — the whole-workspace
233	    administrator, distinct from the per-suite view/edit/admin/owner ladder in
234	    `suite_authz`. Matched case-insensitively on the IdP-supplied email, a
235	    generic identity attribute, so no Azure/Entra claim is read here
236	    (ADR 0010/0013, CLAUDE.md §11). Resolves the allowlist via `get_settings()`
237	    (not the import-time `_settings` singleton) so a test can vary it with
238	    `get_settings.cache_clear()`; in a running process settings are read once at
239	    startup (12-factor — change the env and restart).
240	    """
241	    return get_settings().is_admin_email(user.email)
242	
243	
244	def require_workspace_admin(
245	    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
246	) -> User:
247	    """FastAPI dependency gating the /admin endpoints — 403 for a non-admin.
248	
249	    Server-side authz (never a client toggle): a non-admin gets a real 403, which
250	    the frontend renders as the forbidden page.
251	    """
252	    if not is_workspace_admin(current_user):
253	        raise DataQError(
254	            code="workspace_admin_required",
255	            message="This action requires workspace-admin access.",
256	            status_code=403,
257	        )
258	    return current_user

1	"""Auth for the MCP server — the *same* credentials the REST API accepts.
2	
3	MCP clients (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai / Copilot / Cursor) present either the
4	Azure AD access token the web UI uses **or a DataQ PAT** (`dq_live_…`, ADR 0026
5	— the seam is shared, never MCP-only). Azure tokens are validated with a
6	fastmcp ``JWTVerifier`` configured from the same tenant / audience / scope as
7	``core.auth`` — issuer, signature (Azure JWKS), expiry, and the required API
8	scope; PATs by hashed lookup via ``api_key_service``, exactly like REST. The
9	two are disjoint by prefix, composed in ``_PatOrJwtVerifier``.
10	
11	Two modes, picked from settings exactly like ``core.auth``:
12	
13	- **Real mode** (`azure_auth_configured`): the composite verifier above.
14	- **Dev bypass** (`ENVIRONMENT=dev` + `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true`, no Azure vars): no
15	  verifier — every call resolves to the fixed dev user, for local dev only.
16	
17	If neither is configured the server is **not mounted** (fail-closed — the
18	``/mcp`` endpoint never goes live without auth; CLAUDE.md §10 security note).
19	"""
20	
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	from typing import Any
24	
25	from fastapi_azure_auth.utils import is_guest
26	from fastmcp.server.auth import AccessToken, AuthProvider, TokenVerifier
27	from fastmcp.server.auth.providers.jwt import JWTVerifier
28	from fastmcp.server.dependencies import get_access_token
29	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

36	    _upsert_user,
37	)

40	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
41	from backend.app.db.models import User
42	from backend.app.services import api_key_service
43	
44	log = get_logger(__name__)
45	
46	# Claim key carrying the PAT-resolved DataQ user id through fastmcp's token
47	# context into `resolve_current_user` (a DataQ-internal claim, not an OIDC one).
48	PAT_USER_CLAIM = "dataq_user_id"
49	
50	
51	class McpAuthError(Exception):
52	    """Raised inside a tool when the caller can't be resolved (defence-in-depth)."""
53	
54	
55	def mcp_enabled(settings: Settings | None = None) -> bool:
56	    """Whether ``/mcp`` should be mounted at all — only when auth is resolvable.
57	
58	    Real Azure auth, or the local dev-bypass. Never an unauthenticated mount in a
59	    deployed (prod/staging) environment.
60	    """
61	    s = settings or get_settings()
62	    return s.azure_auth_configured or _dev_bypass_allowed(s)
63	
64	
65	class _PatOrJwtVerifier(TokenVerifier):
66	    """Composite verifier: DataQ PAT by prefix, else the Azure ``JWTVerifier``.
67	
68	    The branches are disjoint (a ``dq_live_…`` bearer is never a valid JWT).
69	    A bad PAT returns ``None`` — fastmcp turns that into the standard 401 —
70	    and is logged prefix-only inside ``api_key_service``.
71	    """
72	
73	    def __init__(self, jwt_verifier: JWTVerifier) -> None:
74	        super().__init__()
75	        self._jwt = jwt_verifier
76	
77	    async def verify_token(self, token: str) -> AccessToken | None:
78	        if not token.startswith(api_key_service.TOKEN_PREFIX):
79	            return await self._jwt.verify_token(token)
80	        from backend.app.db.session import SessionLocal
81	
82	        session = SessionLocal()
83	        try:
84	            user = api_key_service.resolve_token(session, token)
85	        except DataQError:
86	            return None
87	        finally:
88	            session.close()
89	        return AccessToken(
90	            token=token,
91	            client_id="dataq-pat",
92	            scopes=[],
93	            expires_at=None,
94	            claims={PAT_USER_CLAIM: str(user.id)},
95	        )
96	
97	
98	def build_auth_provider(settings: Settings | None = None) -> AuthProvider | None:
99	    """The fastmcp auth provider — PAT-or-Azure-JWT in real mode, ``None`` in dev bypass.
100	
101	    Returning ``None`` leaves the mounted server unauthenticated; callers must only
102	    mount in that case when ``_dev_bypass_allowed`` is true (see ``mcp_enabled``).
103	    """
104	    s = settings or get_settings()
105	    if not s.azure_auth_configured:
106	        return None
107	    tenant = s.azure_tenant_id
108	    # Single-tenant v2 endpoint — same coordinates fastapi-azure-auth uses.
109	    jwt = JWTVerifier(
110	        jwks_uri=f"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/discovery/v2.0/keys",
111	        issuer=f"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/v2.0",
112	        audience=s.azure_api_client_id,
113	        required_scopes=[s.azure_api_scope],
114	    )
115	    return _PatOrJwtVerifier(jwt)
116	
117	
118	def resolve_current_user(session: Session) -> User:
119	    """Resolve the calling user and upsert them — the MCP twin of ``get_current_user``.
120	
121	    In real mode the validated token's claims (set by the ``JWTVerifier``) supply
122	    the AAD object id + email + name, upserted via the shared ``_upsert_user`` so
123	    the ``users`` row is identical to a web-UI login. In dev bypass (no token) the
124	    fixed dev user is used. Reuses ``core.auth`` so claim handling can't drift.
125	    """
126	    token=[REDACTED]()
127	    if token is not None:
128	        claims: dict[str, Any] = token.claims or {}
129	        # PAT path (ADR 0026): the verifier already resolved (and last-used-
130	        # stamped) the owning user; load it by id — no upsert, the user exists.
131	        pat_user_id = claims.get(PAT_USER_CLAIM)
132	        if pat_user_id:
133	            user = session.get(User, pat_user_id)
134	            if user is None:  # revoked/deleted between verify and tool call
135	                raise McpAuthError("could not resolve the API key's user")
136	            return user
137	        # Mirror the REST validator's guest policy: reject Azure AD guests (B2B /
138	        # external) unless explicitly allowed, so /mcp can't accept an identity the
139	        # REST API would 403. The JWTVerifier already validated signature / issuer /
140	        # audience / scope; this is the tenant-membership policy on top.
141	        if not get_settings().azure_allow_guest_users and is_guest(claims):
142	            raise McpAuthError("guest users are not permitted")
143	        # `oid` (the stable directory object id) is mandatory, exactly as the REST
144	        # resolver treats it — never fall back to `sub` (a per-app pairwise
145	        # pseudonym), which would key a divergent / duplicate users row.
146	        aad_oid = claims.get("oid")
147	        if aad_oid:
148	            email = str(
149	                claims.get("preferred_username") or claims.get("email") or claims.get("upn") or ""
150	            )
151	            name = claims.get("name")
152	            return _upsert_user(
153	                session,
154	                aad_object_id=str(aad_oid),
155	                email=email,
156	                display_name=str(name) if name is not None else None,
157	            )
158	    if _dev_bypass_allowed(get_settings()):
159	        return _upsert_user(
160	            session,
161	            aad_object_id=DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID,
162	            email=DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL,
163	            display_name=DEV_BYPASS_DISPLAY_NAME,
164	        )
165	    # Auth provider rejects unauthenticated calls before reaching a tool; this is
166	    # defence-in-depth for the (mis)configured case.
167	    raise McpAuthError("could not resolve an authenticated MCP user")
168

"""Unit tests for the MCP auth module (no DB, no network).

Covers the two operating modes and user resolution: real Azure mode builds a
JWTVerifier from the same tenant/audience/scope as the REST API; dev-bypass and
unconfigured modes build none; and `resolve_current_user` reads the validated
token's claims (or the dev-bypass user).
"""

from types import SimpleNamespace
from typing import Any

import pytest
from fastmcp.server.auth.providers.jwt import JWTVerifier

from backend.app.core.auth import DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID, DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL
from backend.app.core.config import Settings
from backend.app.mcp import auth


def _settings(**kw: Any) -> Settings:
    return Settings(_env_file=None, **kw)


def test_build_auth_provider_real_mode_is_jwt_verifier_for_the_api_app() -> None:
    s = _settings(azure_tenant_id="tenant-1", azure_api_client_id="api-client", environment="prod")
    provider = auth.build_auth_provider(s)
    assert isinstance(provider, JWTVerifier)


def test_build_auth_provider_none_without_azure() -> None:
    assert auth.build_auth_provider(_settings()) is None


def test_mcp_enabled_real_or_dev_bypass_only() -> None:
    assert auth.mcp_enabled(_settings(azure_tenant_id="t", azure_api_client_id="c")) is True
    assert auth.mcp_enabled(_settings(environment="dev", auth_dev_bypass=True)) is True
    # Neither real auth nor dev bypass → not enabled (fail-closed, never unauthenticated).
    assert auth.mcp_enabled(_settings(environment="prod")) is False


def test_resolve_user_from_token_claims(db_session: Any, monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    token = SimpleNamespace(
        claims={"oid": "aad-oid-123", "preferred_username": "ada@acme.io", "name": "Ada"},
        subject="aad-oid-123",
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(auth, "get_access_token", lambda: token)
    user = auth.resolve_current_user(db_session)
    assert user.aad_object_id == "aad-oid-123"
    assert user.email == "ada@acme.io"


def test_resolve_user_rejects_guest_by_default(db_session: Any, monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    """A guest token (acct=1) is rejected unless azure_allow_guest_users — same as REST."""
    token = SimpleNamespace(claims={"oid": "g1", "preferred_username": "g@ext", "acct": 1})
    monkeypatch.setattr(auth, "get_access_token", lambda: token)
    monkeypatch.setattr(auth, "get_settings", lambda: _settings(azure_allow_guest_users=False))
    with pytest.raises(auth.McpAuthError):
        auth.resolve_current_user(db_session)

def test_resolve_user_allows_guest_when_enabled(db_session: Any, monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    token = SimpleNamespace(claims={"oid": "g1", "preferred_username": "g@ext", "acct": 1})
    monkeypatch.setattr(auth, "get_access_token", lambda: token)
    monkeypatch.setattr(auth, "get_settings", lambda: _settings(azure_allow_guest_users=True))
    assert auth.resolve_current_user(db_session).aad_object_id == "g1"


def test_resolve_user_requires_oid_no_subject_fallback(db_session: Any, monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    """A token without `oid` is not silently keyed on the pairwise `sub`."""
    token = SimpleNamespace(claims={"preferred_username": "x@acme.io"}, subject="pairwise-sub")
    monkeypatch.setattr(auth, "get_access_token", lambda: token)
    monkeypatch.setattr(auth, "get_settings", lambda: _settings(environment="prod"))
    with pytest.raises(auth.McpAuthError):
        auth.resolve_current_user(db_session)


def test_resolve_user_dev_bypass_when_no_token(db_session: Any, monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(auth, "get_access_token", lambda: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        auth, "get_settings", lambda: _settings(environment="dev", auth_dev_bypass=True)
    )
    user = auth.resolve_current_user(db_session)
    assert user.aad_object_id == DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID
    assert user.email == DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL


def test_resolve_user_raises_when_unauthenticated_and_no_bypass(
    db_session: Any, monkeypatch: Any
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(auth, "get_access_token", lambda: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(auth, "get_settings", lambda: _settings(environment="prod"))
    with pytest.raises(auth.McpAuthError):

The PAT branch sits in front of\nthe bypass (same seam order as real mode), so presenting `Authorization:\nBearer dq_live_…` must resolve to the key's OWNER — not the dev user — and a\nbad PAT must 401 rather than fall through to the bypass identity.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport uuid\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom backend.app.core.auth import DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL\nfrom backend.app.db.models import User\nfrom backend.app.db.session import get_db\nfrom backend.app.main import app\nfrom backend.app.services import api_key_service as svc\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client(db_session: Any) -> Iterator[TestClient]:\n    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: db_session\n    try:\n        yield TestClient(app)\n    finally:\n        app.dependency_overrides.clear()\n\n\ndef _pat_header(token: str) -> dict[str, str]:\n    return {\"Authorization\": f\"Bearer {token}\"}\n\n\ndef test_mint_returns_token_once_and_list_never_does(client: TestClient) -> None:\n    created = client.post(\"/api/v1/me/api-keys\", json={\"name\": \"ci-smoke\"})\n    assert created.status_code == 201\n    body = created.json()\n    assert body[\"token\"].startswith(svc.TOKEN_PREFIX)\n    assert body[\"name\"] == \"ci-smoke\"\n    assert body[\"key_prefix\"] == body[\"token\"][: len(body[\"key_prefix\"])]\n    assert body[\"revoked_at\"] is None\n\n    listed = client.get(\"/api/v1/me/api-keys\")\n    assert listed.status_code == 200\n    (row,) = listed.json()\n    assert row[\"id\"] == body[\"id\"]\n    assert \"token\" not in row  # metadata only — the plaintext appeared exactly once\n    assert \"key_hash\" not in row\n\n\ndef test_expiry_bounds_are_422(client: TestClient) -> None:\n    assert client.post(\"/api/v1/me/api-keys\", json={\"name\": \"x\", \"expires_in_days\": 0}).status_code == 422\n    assert (\n        client.post(\n            \"/api/v1/me/api-keys\",\n            json={\"name\": \"x\", \"expires_in_days\": svc.MAX_EXPIRY_DAYS + 1},\n        ).status_code\n        == 422\n    )\n\n\ndef test_pat_authenticates_as_its_owner_not_the_bypass_user(\n    client: TestClient, db_session: Any\n) -> None:\n    owner = User(id=uuid.uuid4(), aad_object_id=f\"oid-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}\", email=\"pat@x.io\")\n    db_session.add(owner)\n    db_session.commit()\n    _, token = svc.create_key(db_session, owner, name=\"e2e\")\n\n    body = client.get(\"/api/v1/me\", headers=_pat_header(token)).json()\n    assert body[\"email\"] == \"pat@x.io\"\n    assert body[\"email\"] != DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL\n\n\ndef test_bad_pat_401s_instead_of_falling_through_to_bypass(client: TestClient) -> None:\n    r = client.get(\"/api/v1/me\", headers=_pat_header(svc.TOKEN_PREFIX + \"bogus\"))\n    assert r.status_code == 401\n    assert r.json()[\"error\"][\"code\"] == \"invalid_api_key\"\n\n\ndef test_revoked_pat_stops_authenticating_immediately(client: TestClient) -> None:\n    body = client.post(\"/api/v1/me/api-keys\", json={\"name\": \"doomed\"}).json()\n    token = body[\"token\"]\n    assert client.get(\"/api/v1/me\", headers=_pat_header(token)).status_code == 200\n\n    assert client.delete(f\"/api/v1/me/api-keys/{body['id']}\").status_code == 204\n    assert client.get(\"/api/v1/me\", headers=_pat_header(token)).status_code == 401\n    # Idempotent re-revoke.\n    assert client.delete(f\"/api/v1/me/api-keys/{body['id']}\").status_code == 204\n\n\ndef test_revoking_another_users_key_404s(client: TestClient, db_session: Any) -> None:\n    owner = User(id=uuid.uuid4(), aad_object_id=f\"oid-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}\", email=\"o@x.io\")\n    db_session.add(owner)\n    db_session.commit()\n    key, _ = svc.create_key(db_session, owner, name=\"theirs\")\n\n    r = client.delete(f\"/api/v1/me/api-keys/{key.id}\")\n    assert r.status_code == 404\n\n\ndef test_pat_lifecycle_via_pat_auth_itself(client: TestClient, db_session: Any) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A PAT can manage keys too (it IS the user): mint over PAT auth works.\"\"\"\n    owner = User(id=uuid.uuid4(), aad_object_id=f\"oid-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}\", email=\"s@x.io\")\n    db_session.add(owner)\n    db_session.commit()\n    _, token = svc.create_key(db_session, owner, name=\"root\")\n\n    r = client.post(\"/api/v1/me/api-keys\", json={\"name\": \"child\"}, headers=_pat_header(token))\n    assert r.status_code == 201\n    names = {k[\"name\"] for k in client.get(\"/api/v1/me/api-keys\", headers=_pat_header(token)).json()}\n    assert names == {\"root\", \"child\"}\n"
}

1	# ADR 0026 — DataQ-issued API keys / service tokens behind the auth seam (REST + MCP)
2	
3	- **Status:** Proposed — **build deferred to post-v1** (timing decision recorded 2026-07-03; see Decision record below)
4	- **Date:** 2026-06-29 (timing decided 2026-07-03)
5	- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
6	- **Related:** ADR [0010](0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md) (the `get_current_user` identity seam — Azure is one impl, not the architecture), [0013](0013-marketplace-distribution-and-anti-lock-in.md) (BYOL / anti-lock-in), [0008](0008-mcp-server.md) (MCP auth via `JWTVerifier` — bring-your-own-token today), [0020](0020-history-and-audit-strategy.md) (audit), compliance posture (#436)
7	- **Issue:** [#461](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/461)
8	
9	> **Stub — Proposed, not yet designed in full.** Captures the direction while it's fresh; to be fleshed out when Theme 3 (access/identity) is picked up post-v1.
10	
11	## Context
12	
13	Authentication today is **exclusively Azure AD bearer tokens** (delegated/SSO) for both the REST API and `/mcp`. There is no DataQ-native credential. Two problems follow:
14	
15	1. **Lock-in.** This is the deepest remaining Azure coupling. The `get_current_user` seam (ADR 0010) exists and service code never reads Entra claims (CLAUDE.md §11), but the seam has exactly *one* real implementation, and the persistence layer is still Azure-shaped (`users.aad_object_id`). A BYOL customer on AWS/GCP (ADR 0013) has no Azure AD and cannot authenticate at all.
16	2. **No programmatic access.** Headless agents, CI, and always-on MCP clients want a long-lived, scoped, revocable secret — not a ~60-min Azure token they must refresh (ADR 0008 uses a token-*validating* `JWTVerifier`, not a client-driven OAuth provider). There is no API-key / PAT / service-token mechanism.
17	
18	## Decision (direction — to be detailed)
19	
20	Introduce a **DataQ-issued credential as a second authenticator behind the existing `get_current_user` seam**, so the **REST API and `/mcp` accept it identically** — explicitly *not* an MCP-only feature. On MCP, fastmcp `MultiAuth` lets `/mcp` accept either a DataQ key or an Azure token. Adding a second real auth impl is also what *exercises* (and thereby validates) the seam ADR 0010 describes.
21	
22	**Phased:**
23	
24	1. **User-scoped PATs first.** A key belongs to a user and inherits that user's per-suite grants → **no new authz model** (reuse the `view < edit < admin < owner` ladder; optionally down-scope a key to read-only — ideal for MCP read tools / dashboards, smallest blast radius). ~80% of the value for a fraction of the change.
25	2. **Service-account principals later.** These force the larger move and should be sequenced after PATs prove the seam: generalize `users.aad_object_id` into a generic **principal** with pluggable identity bindings (Azure AD oid, API key, …), and extend suite **sharing** to non-user principals.
26	
27	**Credential bar (this is a new secret surface — not to be half-built):**
28	
29	- Hash-at-rest (argon2/bcrypt), **show-once** on creation, identifying prefix (`dq_live_…`), expiry defaults, revocation, last-used + audit.
30	- Hashes live in a **new `api_keys` table** — *not* the credential SecretStore (that store is for *retrievable* connection secrets; a key hash is a verifier secret, never retrievable).
31	- **Lifecycle tied to the owner**: deactivating a user kills their keys, so a PAT can't become an SSO-policy backdoor that outlives the account.
32	- Never logged (prefix only) — same discipline as the compliance posture (#436).
33	
34	## Decision record (2026-07-03 — the go-live "now vs post-v1" call)
35	
36	**Deferred to post-v1 (Theme 3).** Rationale: this is a credential surface with an explicit
37	do-not-half-build bar, and v1's actual programmatic needs are covered by interim mechanisms —
38	the Azure CLI is pre-authorized on the API scope (#565: non-interactive
39	`az account get-access-token` bearers for the live-smoke lane and local MCP clients), and
40	`/mcp` accepts the same Azure token as REST (ADR 0008). Rushing a PAT store into go-live week
41	buys little and risks the exact half-build this ADR warns against.
42	
43	**Shape confirmed** (evaluated against alternatives when the timing was decided):
44	
45	- **User-scoped PATs first** — as phased above. Inherits the per-suite ladder, zero new
46	  authz model, revocable per-integration.
47	- **Standalone service accounts later** — the real need is automation that outlives a person
48	  (owner deactivated → their PATs correctly die), but first-class service principals force the
49	  `users.aad_object_id` → generic-principal migration + non-user sharing; sequence after PATs.
50	  Interim escape hatch: a dedicated service user (e.g. `dataq-admin`) owns automation keys.
51	- **HTTP Basic auth — rejected.** DataQ has no password store (identity is delegated to OIDC);
52	  Basic auth would make DataQ a password system (storage/hashing policy, lockout, reset flows,
53	  credential-stuffing surface) for a *worse* credential: one secret per account (revoking one
54	  integration breaks all), no scoping, no expiry, replayed on every request, and routinely
55	  leaked via logs/proxies. A PAT has the same `Authorization`-header ergonomics without any
56	  of that.
57	
58	## Consequences (anticipated)
59	
60	- Discharges the identity-seam lock-in (ADR 0010/0013): Azure AD becomes *one* authenticator behind the seam, not the only one — unblocking BYOL on non-Azure clouds.
61	- Closes the programmatic-access gap for REST automation and headless MCP clients without weakening the per-user authz model (PAT phase).
62	- Adds a credential-management surface (issue/list/revoke UI + API) and an audit obligation.
63	
64	## Open questions (for the full ADR)
65	
66	- Token format + verification cost (hash lookup on every request — caching?).
67	- Scope granularity: read-only vs read-write vs per-suite.
68	- Where service-account principals sit relative to the workspace-admin allowlist.
69	- Migration path for `users.aad_object_id` → generic principal without breaking existing ownership/shares.
70	
```

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/docs/api-keys.md",
  "content": "# API keys (personal access tokens)\n\nDataQ can mint you a **personal access token (PAT)** — a long-lived, revocable\ncredential for scripts, CI, and always-on MCP clients, where an SSO browser\nflow or a ~60-minute Azure AD token doesn't fit (ADR\n[0026](adr/0026-auth-api-keys-and-principal-seam.md)).\n\nA PAT authenticates **as you**: it inherits exactly your per-suite access\n(`view < edit < admin < owner`) on the REST API and `/mcp` alike. There is no\nseparate \"API-key permission model\" to configure — if you can see a suite in\nthe web app, your key can; if you can't, it can't.\n\n## Minting a key\n\n`POST /api/v1/me/api-keys` (any authenticated caller — including an existing\nPAT):\n\n```bash\ncurl -sS -X POST \"$DATAQ_URL/api/v1/me/api-keys\" \\\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $AZURE_AD_TOKEN\" \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -d '{\"name\": \"ci-smoke\", \"expires_in_days\": 90}'\n```\n\nThe response carries the plaintext token **exactly once**:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"…\",\n  \"name\": \"ci-smoke\",\n  \"key_prefix\": \"dq_live_AbCd\",\n  \"expires_at\": \"2026-10-02T09:00:00Z\",\n  \"token\": \"dq_live_…\"\n}\n```\n\n!!! danger \"Store it now — it cannot be retrieved again\"\n    Only a hash is kept at rest. If the token is lost, revoke the key and mint\n    a new one. Never commit a token to version control; put it in your CI\n    secret store / Key Vault.\n\n- `name` — a label for telling keys apart (e.g. `ci-smoke`, `mcp-desktop`).\n- `expires_in_days` — default **90**, maximum **365**. Non-expiring keys are\n  not supported.\n\n## Using a key\n\nThe token goes wherever an Azure AD bearer would — same header, same\nendpoints:\n\n```bash\ncurl -sS \"$DATAQ_URL/api/v1/suites\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer dq_live_…\"\n```\n\nFor MCP clients, use it in place of the short-lived browser token in your\nclient config (see [AI assistants (MCP setup)](mcp-setup.md)) — no more\nre-pasting on 401s until the key expires.\n\n## Listing and revoking\n\n```bash\ncurl -sS \"$DATAQ_URL/api/v1/me/api-keys\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer …\"\ncurl -sS -X DELETE \"$DATAQ_URL/api/v1/me/api-keys/<key_id>\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer …\"\n```\n\nListing returns metadata only (name, prefix, expiry, last-used) — never the\ntoken. Revocation (`DELETE`, 204) is immediate and idempotent: the key stops\nauthenticating on its next request. Mint one key **per integration** so\nrevoking one doesn't break the others.\n\n## Security properties\n\n| Property | Behaviour |\n|---|---|\n| At rest | SHA-256 hash only; the plaintext is never stored or logged (prefix only) |\n| Show-once | Plaintext appears solely in the creation response |\n| Expiry | Mandatory (≤ 365 days); expired keys stop authenticating |\n| Revocation | Immediate, per-key, idempotent |\n| Failure mode | Unknown, revoked, and expired keys all return the **same** 401 — no probing oracle |\n| Owner lifecycle | Deleting/deactivating a user kills their keys with them |\n| Last used | `last_used_at` tracked (coarse-grained) for spotting stale keys |\n"
}
```

```
    `/mcp` answers with a **307 redirect** to `/mcp/`, and some HTTP clients drop the
    `Authorization` header when following redirects — which then surfaces as a
    confusing 401. Always configure clients with the `/mcp/` form.

The endpoint is **Azure AD–protected**: present the same bearer token the web UI uses (validated against the same tenant / audience / scope). Without auth configured, the endpoint is only mounted in local dev-bypass mode — never unauthenticated in a deployed environment (ADR [0008](adr/0008-mcp-server.md)).

### Getting a token

Sign in to the DataQ web app, open your browser's developer tools → **Application → Session Storage** → the `oidc.user:…` entry → copy the `access_token` value.

!!! note "Tokens expire after ~1 hour"
    The pasted token is short-lived; when the client starts getting 401s, paste a
    fresh one and restart the MCP server/connection. Long-lived DataQ-issued API
    keys for headless MCP configs are tracked in ADR 0026
    ([#461](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/461)).

!!! danger "Never commit a config that carries a token"
    Keep token-bearing MCP config files out of version control (in the DataQ repo
    itself, `.gitignore` already covers `.vscode/*`).
```

{
  "replace_all": false,
